# DAILY (after market close)

## D1. Market Development Scan — deep research

```
**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='D1' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed' AND DATETIME(log_ts,'America/Denver') >= DATETIME(<today, America/Denver>, TIME '12:00:00')` (noon-threshold clause — D1 is EVENING-slot daily, so count ONLY completions logged in the real evening window; a post-midnight prior-day run mis-stamped onto today by bigquery/12's midnight-crossing grace has an early-AM `log_ts` and is correctly EXCLUDED, so it can't cancel today's genuine evening run — see the shared Observability guard's CYCLE-AWARE VARIANT); if `>= 1`, output "D1 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or D1's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-scan, do NOT re-overwrite `Daily.md`, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

Read access scope: Daily cadence. Query `events.decision_log` (+ `analytics.find_precedents()`) bounded to the recent operationally-relevant window — `events.decision_log` holds all history, queryable, no live/archive split (§15). Read factbase files (`B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`) per prompt direction.

Read Strategy.md, Experiment_Parameters.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md, Watchlist.md, Operating_Protocols.md (positions from `state.current_positions`, regime from `state.current_regime`, decisions from `events.decision_log`).

Read `state.current_positions` to identify currently-open positions across Strategies A, B, C, D, E with their entry-record thesis-invalidation criteria. Read Watchlist.md for queued names.

Apply the shared 'NO-GO records are context, not barriers' rule when any candidate has a prior `events.decision_log` NO-GO entry.

Produce a daily market development scan and write it directly to `Daily.md` (overwrite; first line = today's calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format).

SCAN WINDOW — dynamic, measured from the last D1 run to now (not a fixed lookback). Set the window start = the timestamp through which the previous D1 scan covered, and scan all developments from there to now (this run's execution time, America/Denver). Resolve the start automatically, in priority order:

1. **Prior Daily.md stamp (primary).** At run start, `Daily.md` on disk is still the previous run's output (this run overwrites it). Read it first and parse the machine-readable marker `<!-- d1_scan_through_utc: <ISO-8601 UTC> -->` written just below the date line by the previous run — that timestamp is the exact hand-off boundary → window start.
2. **Git commit timestamp (fallback + cross-check).** If the marker is missing or unparseable, use the commit time of the most recent `Daily.md` commit — `git log -1 --format=%cI -- Daily.md` (every D1 run commits Daily.md as "D1 Market Development Scan …"). Also use this to sanity-check (1); the two should agree to within one session's length.
3. **Conservative fixed lookback (last resort).** If neither is available (e.g. a shallow clone with no Daily.md history, or no prior file at all), fall back to a 30-hour lookback ending now. Never silently narrow coverage below this.

This keeps coverage gap-free across skipped or delayed runs: if a scheduled run was missed, the window automatically stretches back to the *actual* last run instead of dropping a session (e.g. the 2026-06-06 run correctly had to cover the Friday 6/5 session because there was no D1 between Thu 6/4 and Sat 6/6 — a fixed 24-hour lookback would have missed all of Friday). If the resolved start is more than ~50 hours ago (a multi-session gap), state the gap explicitly in the scan-window line; always cover at least the most recent completed trading session even when the elapsed window is short. Throughout DEVELOPMENTS below, "today" means "within this scan window" (≥ today; more when the window spans a missed run).

Record the boundary for the next run: in the Daily.md you write, emit `<!-- d1_scan_through_utc: <this run's execution time, ISO-8601 UTC> -->` on the line directly below the date, and a human-readable `Scan window: <start · America/Denver> → <now · America/Denver>` line in the header.

Cast broadly — do not scope the scan to tickers owned or on the watchlist. The purpose is to surface any development that could either threaten an existing position's thesis or create a new entry opportunity for any strategy, including at names not currently on any list. Do not pad; if a category has no material items, state so.

TL;DR (readability — added 2026-07). Immediately after the header (scan-window line + tape summary), before DEVELOPMENTS, write a ≤6-line plain-bullet TL;DR: exits triggered (count + tickers, or "none"), new entry candidates (count + tickers, or "none"), add candidates (count + tickers, or "none" — Rev 40 A/B/D adds, see ANALYSIS — ADD-CANDIDATE CHECK below), watchlist changes (or "none"), and a one-line regime-review flag (or "no review"). This is a summary of the RECOMMENDED ACTIONS section computed below, placed at the top for a human skimming top-down (D2 still reads the full file bottom-up as today; this changes nothing D2 parses).

SEARCH PROTOCOL — WIDEN THE FIRST SEARCH BEFORE ISSUING A SECOND ON THE SAME SUBJECT (added 2026-08-21, external-spend audit; the concrete per-cluster form of the shared "Metered external calls" rule's part (b), which already records that `max_results`, `chunks_per_source`, `topic`, `time_range` and `include_domains` are ALL free and that "widening a single search always beats issuing a second one"). Before issuing a SECOND search on a subject you have already searched THIS run, re-issue the FIRST search wider — raise `max_results`, widen `time_range`/`start_date`/`end_date`, add or relax `include_domains` — instead of adding a narrower sibling query. None of those parameters touches the bill (a search returning 20 results bills identically to one returning 5), so one wide re-issue retires a whole subject for one credit where a chain of narrow siblings bills once per link. MEASURED, D1's own 2026-08-20 run: of 71 logged search targets in `ops.web_calls`, **36 (51%) fell into six subject clusters** — Intuitive Surgical / da Vinci / CMR Surgical ×8 (all advanced, 16 credits), a per-ticker `<NAME> stock news August 20 2026` sweep ×~15, crypto/XRP ×5, steel/tariff ×4, plus Alibaba ×2 and Nordson ×2. Collapsing each cluster to ~2 wide searches would have removed ~22 searches at that run's 1.76 credits/search average, ~39 credits or ~31% of the run (an ESTIMATE off one run's targets — the fleet-wide figure is not measurable until every routine logs its calls). **This is NOT a per-run search cap and NOT a bar on follow-up searches**, and it narrows nothing about what may be consulted (§"Evidence lists are floors, not ceilings"): the Intuitive Surgical cluster went from "why did it drop" to a named competitor's FDA clearance, a real chain of inference and exactly the evidence quality the owner has said is worth paying for. What it targets is the narrower SIBLING that re-asks a question already asked. Per the shared rule's part (d), nothing here sets a per-routine credit cap, and none follows from spend alone. **FAN-OUT LIMB — WHO HOLDS THE RUN-LEVEL SUBJECT LEDGER (added 2026-10-18, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D1's `d1_single_session_rules_not_inherited_by_subagents`, alert `959693b5-5cfa-4583-ad21-57f3bfcbce84`).** The protocol's pronoun is "you" and its unit is "this run"; when D1 runs as an orchestrator plus sub-agents those come apart, because no sub-agent sees another's queries. MEASURED 2026-09-24: 73 metered calls in one run; the single-name-move screen sub-agent made 39 against a ~10 brief (29 Tavily, all per-NAME narrower siblings across 8 subjects: MGM x5, INTC x4, ORCL x4, SECZ x4, DRI x3, GRAL x2, TWST x2, IONQ x1) and the developments-scan sub-agent 29 against ~12 — with the rule quoted verbatim in both briefs, so this is not a prompt omission. **When D1 fans out, the ORCHESTRATOR owns the ledger: (i) it assigns each sub-agent a disjoint set of subjects and the brief forbids searching outside that set, and (ii) the brief states a per-SUBJECT call cap (a single global budget is unenforceable by an agent that cannot see the others spend).** Still NOT a per-run search cap and NOT a bar on follow-up searches — the target remains the redundant narrower sibling, and a chain that is genuinely advancing (the Intuitive Surgical precedent) is exempt.

DEVELOPMENTS

1. Market-wide breaking events. Geopolitical shocks, unscheduled regulatory or enforcement actions, material bankruptcies, disasters, or events materially affecting global risk assets. Per event: what happened, source, observable reaction across equities / rates / commodities / FX.

2. Scheduled events that resolved today (across the US-listed universe with market cap ≥ $2B, not limited to watchlist). Earnings prints (EPS/revenue vs. consensus), FDA PDUFA outcomes, FOMC actions, other resolved catalysts. Per event: outcome, price reaction if observable, source. **ENUMERATION SOURCE PIN (added 2026-10-20, interactive triage of D1's `fmp_earnings_calendar_empty_for_window` warning, `ops.alerts` `638b4521`):** enumerate the day's scheduled earnings from Nasdaq's key-less calendar — `curl` `https://api.nasdaq.com/api/calendar/earnings?date=<YYYY-MM-DD>` with a browser User-Agent; never `WebFetch`, which returns a model's reading rather than bytes and cannot set a User-Agent. `data.rows[]` carries `symbol`, `name`, `marketCap` (a `$`-formatted string), `time` (`time-pre-market` / `time-after-hours` / `time-not-supplied`), `epsForecast`, `noOfEsts`, `fiscalQuarterEnding` — filter to `marketCap >= $2B`, one fetch per scan-window day. Key-less and unmetered, it owes NO `ops.web_calls` row (the obligation below covers Tavily/HF/FMP calls). FMP `calendar/earnings-calendar` is NOT an enumeration source: it carries a SPARSE MEGA-CAP SUBSET. Keep FMP for per-event consensus on names it carries; do not re-raise `fmp_earnings_calendar_empty_for_window` for an empty short window, the expected answer when its subset has no reporter. The EVENT-IDENTITY GATE binds unchanged. **EVENT-IDENTITY GATE (earnings and any event-dependent position/invalidation assessment):** before recording results or marking any criterion assessed against an event, verify from the primary issuer/authority source that it occurred within this D1 scan window; record the source's release date/time and stated fiscal period. A calendar date is a schedule, never evidence of a completed print. Never relabel an older release as the current fiscal period because figures resemble an expected result. If the primary result is unpublished, record only pending (with confirmed scheduled date), omit outcome figures and affirmative event-dependent assessments, and queue/re-run after publication. Replace a wrong prior event record append-only with `ops.sp_log_decision(... in_superseded_by=<old entry_id>)`; never UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE the original. **FAN-OUT RECONCILIATION:** when D1 runs as orchestrator plus sub-agents, the ORCHESTRATOR must, before composing DEVELOPMENTS, reconcile differing leg identifications (date, fiscal period, outcome) against the primary issuer/authority source and record that issuer source. Compare the legs' event lists by (ticker, event date) before writing; do not rely on ticker overlap to expose contradictions. **FDA LIMB — RESOLVE SPONSOR AND STATUS AGAINST THE FDA'S OWN APPROVALS / CRL PAGE BEFORE NAMING EITHER, never against an aggregator calendar alone.** Treat forward PDUFA listings for already-approved drugs and same-brand/different-sponsor pairings as suspect. Record any PDUFA row unresolved against the FDA's own page as unresolved, never a dated forward action. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-01.)*

3. Large single-name moves — **AI-SIGNIFICANCE SCREEN (Operating_Protocols.md §19, owner-approved redesign 2026-07-19; loop `research_screener`).** Layer-1 population rail (mechanical cost bound, never significance): US-listed equities with market cap ≥ $2B that moved ≥2% close-to-close today attributable to identifiable public events — **every close-to-close figure is measured from IBKR regular-session daily bars (`get_price_history`, `step='ONE_DAY'`, `outside_rth=false`), NEVER from `get_price_snapshot`; Operating_Protocols.md §19 PRICE BASIS.** **AND THE MOVE IS READ FROM THE BAR SERIES' `close` ARRAY AT BOTH ENDS — never `open`, never `high`/`low`, never a midpoint.** The tool returns parallel `time`/`open`/`high`/`low`/`close`/`volume` arrays: the correct call alone does not validate the selected array. **SOURCE-DISAGREEMENT RULE (§19):** a third-party close that disagrees with yours is evidence against YOUR read until you re-derive it. A snapshot's `last` can be after-hours and cross Strategy B's frozen ≥5% spec floor (plus up to 3 sub-net items judged extraordinary, §19's escape valve). **DISCOVERY AND CONFIRMATION ARE SEPARATE LEGS WITH SEPARATE SOURCES — a DISCOVERY-side outage must never zero this screen.** Discovery finds names; confirmation measures moves and is source-bound to IBKR by §19 PRICE BASIS. **IBKR SHOWED NO SYMBOL-LEVEL GATING ON THE NAMES TESTED — stated as the bounded measurement it is, not as a universal.** Do not assume coverage for OTC/pink-sheet, thinly-traded microcap, freshly-IPO'd or delisted names; measure when encountered. Nothing depends on universal coverage: §19 already mandates IBKR. **BUT THAT ESCALATION PATH DOES NOT ACTUALLY CARRY A MARKET CAP — USE `mcp__FMP__company` `profile-symbol` INSTEAD.** `mcp__FMP__secFilings` `sec-company-full-profile`/`search-by-symbol` can return for symbols denied by `quote`/`company`/`chart`, but carries registrant/SIC/CIK metadata, no `marketCap` or share count. For a symbol dropped by `company/batch-market-cap` or denied by `company/market-cap` or `company/shares-float`, **go to `profile-symbol` FIRST for a cap on a denied symbol.** Do not re-probe this settled FMP TIER MATRIX surface each run. Its implied share count can lag a recent issuance: do not trust magnitude to better than ~±30% for a recently issued name, and second-source any name within ~30% of the rail. **BINDING CONSEQUENCE: never drop a discovered candidate for want of “a second source” while IBKR is up. IBKR IS the source of record here**; third-party quote staleness and FMP tier denial cannot invalidate a figure neither is permitted to supply. **When usual discovery legs are down, `mcp__FMP__marketPerformance` `most-active` is open on the free tier and ranked by VOLUME, not percent move.** `biggest-gainers`/`biggest-losers` are percent-ranked top-50 tail radar dominated by micro-caps/leveraged ETFs. **This does NOT reopen the settled enumeration finding**: 50 volume leaders without a market-cap field are a PARTIAL net, never the ≥$2B/≥2% population; use the partial rather than report an unmeasured zero. **REPORTING RULE: `surfaced_count=0` is reserved for a genuinely QUIET TAPE and must never be written for an UNMEASURED one.** On degraded runs, `surfaced_count` is what you confirmed via IBKR; name failed discovery legs in the decision_log record and `Daily.md`, and name every discovered but unconfirmed candidate individually with its reason. State an unmeasured population explicitly. Layer-2 decides: JUDGE each surfaced name in its own volatility regime and event context per §19; judgment decides the write-up. Per name written up: ticker, move magnitude/direction, **the two `close` values (`prior_close`, `event_close` — §19 RECORD THE TWO PRICES; they must reproduce `metric_pct`)**, event type, source, significance conviction (30/45/60/75) + one-sentence reason, `legacy_rule_pass` (move ≥5%, mechanical record-only benchmark), and `below_spec_floor` for <5% (context/SL1 evidence only — never a B candidate, §19). Log ONE `entry_type='research-screen'` decision_log row (screen='single-name-move') per §19, including quiet days (`surfaced_count=0`, empty arrays). *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-02.)*

   **FIELDS-JSON KEY CONTRACT — THESE EXACT KEY NAMES, EVERY RUN (pinned 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing W2's `screen_fields_schema_drift`).** Use the JSON keys read by `state.research_screen_calls`, which W5's RESEARCH-SCREEN SCORECARD consumes. Do NOT normalise conforming rows toward a nonconforming majority.
   - **Per-item keys, exactly:** `name` (ticker — NOT `ticker`), `metric_pct` (signed close-to-close move — NOT `move_pct`), `conviction_pct` (numeric 30/45/60/75 significance conviction — NOT `conviction`, NOT `significance_conviction`), `reason` (one-sentence judgment — NOT `driver`), `below_spec_floor` (bool), `legacy_rule_pass` (bool), **`prior_close`** and **`event_close`** (the two `close` values used for `metric_pct`; required on `single-name-move`/`sector-move`, omitted on `pair-divergence`; must reproduce `metric_pct` as `(event_close/prior_close − 1) × 100`), plus **`market_cap_usd`** and **`qualifying_event_date`** to make population-rail clearance and event anchors durable.
   - **Top-level keys, exactly:** **`routine` (`"D1"` or `"M2"` — the writing routine, ALWAYS)**, `population_rail`, `legacy_rule`, and agreement counts. `state.research_screen_calls.routine` is `JSON_VALUE(fields,'$.routine')` (`bigquery/96`, `bigquery/122`); `source_session` free text does not supply it. **THE AGREEMENT COUNTS ARE A NESTED OBJECT, NOT THREE FLAT KEYS.** The operative view is `state.research_screen_calls` redefined by `bigquery/122_decision_correction_append_only.sql`, superseding `bigquery/96_research_screener.sql`; it reads `SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(fields,'$.agreement.both') AS INT64) AS agreement_both`, likewise `$.agreement.ai_only`, `$.agreement.rule_only`. **Write `"agreement": {"both": n, "ai_only": n, "rule_only": n}`**, as in `bigquery/96`'s header. A flat top-level `agreement_both` is unread and lands NULL. Per-item keys above ARE flat and match their parser names.
   - **Why it is not cosmetic:** W5's screens-rejecting-winners check is **name-keyed and cannot key on NULL**. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-03.)*

   **PRIOR QUALIFYING SESSIONS IN THE WINDOW — REPORT THEM PER SURFACED B CANDIDATE (added 2026-10-18, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D2's `d1_screen_omits_prior_qualifying_moves_in_window`, alert `3c755d0b-b9aa-4192-a7b1-5e0df21e0b05`).** A screen that reports one qualifying session without the others in the same window hands a thesis session a name that looks like a clean event reaction and is not. MEASURED: D1 surfaced SECZ on 2026-09-24 (+15.1114%) alone; D2 found FIVE ≥5% sessions inside 09-15..09-24 (09-17 +14.9421%, 09-18 +21.6125%, 09-21 +24.3094%, 09-23 +10.4615%, 09-24 +15.1114%; 7.77 → 16.53, +112.7%) with no identified event behind four of them — which prejudices Strategy B criteria 2 and 4 (over/under-shoot and information-vs-sentiment) and also what cleared the $2B cap rail. **For each item surfaced as a Strategy B candidate, count the OTHER ≥5% close-to-close sessions within the candidate's own 10-trading-day window and write `prior_qualifying_sessions` (integer) plus `prior_qualifying_dates` (list) in the item; state it in `reason` when non-zero.** It costs nothing: the same `get_price_history` daily-bar call already made for the close-to-close read takes a wider range for free, and the closes are read from the `close` array as above. Additive; changes no rail or gate. Distinct from `b_intake_population_coverage_unquantified` (which NAMES are measured).

   **`surfaced_count` IS `ARRAY_LENGTH(passed)`, NOT THE LAYER-1 RAIL TALLY — pinned 2026-08-30 by D1, closing W2's `screen_surfaced_count_array_mismatch` finding (`ops.alerts` `da469b47`).** That finding measured D1's 2026-08-24 row `4d30f5d9` carrying `surfaced_count = 25` against a `passed[]` of 17, and correctly could not tell from the row alone whether 8 names had been LOST during the write or the scalar had been taken from a pre-filter tally. **It was the tally, and nothing was lost** — the 2026-08-24 `Daily.md` states it in its own words ("Of the 79, 29 moved ≥2%; **25 of those cleared the $2B cap rail**") and enumerates the 17 Layer-2 passes plus 5 `rejected_notable`. So this is a CONTRACT ambiguity, not data loss, and the ambiguity is the defect: `bigquery/96_research_screener.sql` parses the scalar and the per-item arrays into the SAME view, and W5's RESEARCH-SCREEN SCORECARD reads the scalar as D1's surfacing rate — so a rail tally there overstates surfacing by exactly the names Layer-2 declined, and `analytics.research_screen_disagreements` joins per-item and finds no rows for them. **Therefore: `surfaced_count` counts what this screen SURFACED — the Layer-2 passes written up, i.e. the length of `passed[]` — and the two must agree in every row.** Put the Layer-1 population arithmetic in `fields.rail_tally` (names clearing the mechanical ≥2% + ≥$2B + identified-event rail) and `fields.universe_measured` (how many distinct names this run actually measured), where it is a separate, honestly-named number rather than a second meaning for the same key. **ALSO WRITE `fields.selection_rule` — one line stating HOW the measured names were chosen out of the eligible universe (added 2026-09-20 by D1, adopting W2's `b_intake_population_coverage_unquantified` proposal, `ops.alerts` `08582955`; purely additive, changes no rail and no gate).** `universe_measured` on its own is a numerator with no stated denominator, and because W2's Strategy-B intake is exclusively this durable screen record, D1's bounded scan **IS** the definition of the B candidate population. W2 measured the consequence inside a 21-name sample it already held for other reasons: **24 close-to-close moves ≥5% across the five sessions D1 screened that week appear in NEITHER `passed` NOR `rejected_notable`** — more absent than present (21). A scan bounded by metered-call cost is legitimate and is not being widened here; an UNDESCRIBED one cannot be reported as a coverage ratio by any downstream scorecard, which is the actual defect. The REPORTING RULE above is unchanged and still governs the degraded case: on a degraded run `surfaced_count` is what you actually confirmed via IBKR, which is the same rule read through this definition, not a competing one.

   **CROSS-ROW CLOSE-CHAIN CHECK — RUN IT BEFORE THE INITIAL APPEND; FREE, NO PRICE PULL (added 2026-09-27, closing `d1_below_spec_floor_contradicts_own_anchor_prose`, `ops.alerts` warning `62775339-002b-4e12-8119-45409a6c4f01`).** Full contract in Operating_Protocols.md §19 CROSS-ROW CLOSE CHAIN TEST; the write-time obligation is this. For every item with a real `qualifying_event_date`, read the durable record for any OTHER item carrying the SAME name (`COALESCE($.name, $.ticker)` — both spellings exist historically) and the SAME `qualifying_event_date`, and compare closes numerically: your `prior_close` equal to that item's `event_close` — or your `event_close` equal to its `prior_close` — is a **CHAIN HIT**, and it proves your pair measures the session immediately after the one that item measured. One query covers the whole screen, so this costs one read per run. Resolve every hit against the release's own timing, never against the other item: an after-close anchor legitimately chains forward and is simply recorded in `reason`; a hit on an **intraday or pre-open** anchor means the pair was taken a session late, and the item may not be written until the pair is re-taken on the session the anchor implies and `metric_pct` / `below_spec_floor` are recomputed from it. A hit never aborts the screen. **This is also the mechanism by which one anchor gets screened twice, and nothing in this screen prevents it:** IONQ was recorded for anchor 2026-09-23 on BOTH 09-23 (`91b1a00c`, 40.74 → 42.54, `below_spec_floor=true`) and 09-24 (`6e179f3c`, 42.54 → 44.98, `false`), with the verdict flipped between them and the second item's own `reason` agreeing with the first. If a chain hit lands on an item for a name already dispositioned on this anchor, carry the earlier disposition forward or supersede it explicitly — never write a second, silently disagreeing one. **Coverage is 32% (17 of 53 pair-carrying items have any counterpart, measured 2026-09-27), so a clean pass is not a clearance**, and this check does NOT decide which session `below_spec_floor` is computed on — that is the separate, already-open notice `06c3b0db` against the ANCHOR CONVENTION limb above, adjudication W5.

   **Late-data discipline:** immediately before this initial append, re-read the relevant final state (including any D2a reconciliation that overlapped this D1) and compose the record from that read. If a fact changes after append, `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` for a complete replacement that preserves `entry_type='research-screen'`, carries tag `correction`, and passes `in_superseded_by=<old entry_id>`; never UPDATE, DELETE, or MERGE `events.decision_log`.

   **WRITE PATH — EVERY `research-screen` ROW (BOTH SCREENS, AND ANY CORRECTION OF ONE) IS A GENERATED, DIGEST-CHECKED CALL (added 2026-10-29, interactive triage of D1's `decision_log_large_call_retyped_in_transit`, `ops.alerts` `e1eeeee2`).** Save the row's arguments as a JSON file in the scratch directory — keys are `ops.sp_log_decision`'s argument names without `in_` (`entry_date`, `entry_type`, `title`, `body_md`, `fields` as a JSON object, `tags`, `superseded_by`, `source_session`, …) — then run `python3 scripts/decision_call.py <S>/<screen>.json --out <S>/<screen>` and issue the generated files VERBATIM in the order below, ending with `<S>/<screen>/call.sql`. An unsplit call invokes `ops.sp_log_decision_checked` (`bigquery/270`); a split call assembles its staged parts and delegates to that same procedure (`bigquery/271`). It recomputes the SHA-256 of what BigQuery received against the digest the script embedded, writes through `ops.sp_log_decision` only on a match, and returns `(entry_id, outcome, sha256)`. A `REFUSED, digest mismatch` error means the text was damaged in transit and NOTHING was written: re-issue the same `call.sql`, never an edited copy, and never fall back to a hand-typed `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`. A re-issue after a lost response is safe — the procedure returns the already-landed row as `outcome='already_present'` instead of a duplicate — but if unsure whether a call landed, run `<S>/<screen>/readback.sql` first. A `REFUSED, in_fields_json is not a JSON object` error is a source-file defect: fix the JSON file and regenerate. The landed row carries an extra tag `sha256:<digest>` appended by the procedure; that is its provenance marker, not drift. Files are capped at 24,000 characters and larger rows are split; every literal is wrapped into adjacent pieces of at most 400 characters on their own lines (GoogleSQL concatenates them), so read each file whole and send it whole; never re-compose it from memory or a summary. **Bounded retries:** re-issue a refused call at most TWICE; if the third attempt is also refused, stop, write nothing by any other path, raise the in-run issue `research_screen_write_refused` (§IN-RUN ISSUE REPORTING) naming the screen and the last `received` digest, and say so in the run note — a missing screen row is recoverable next run, while a hand-typed one is the defect this closes. MEASURED 2026-10-28: the ~50KB single-name screen CALL was re-typed by the issuing sub-agent and row 72e9607d landed a wrong fanout date and a dropped legend key, caught only by an improvised per-key readback and replaced append-only by c8a50e56; `ops.sp_log_decision` checks no digest, and its `SAFE.PARSE_JSON` stores `fields = NULL` without an error if the damage breaks the JSON. This is the same control the NEWS-REACTION PAPER BOOK's WRITE INTEGRITY uses for its rows.

   **SPLIT WRITE — ISSUE EACH PART BEFORE THE FINAL CALL (added 2026-10-29, interactive triage of D1's `research_screen_call_issuer_output_truncated`, `ops.alerts` `3e8b19b0`).** MEASURED: on 2026-10-29 the 85,925-byte and 66,399-byte calls were truncated at ~30-45KB of agent output; the row landed at 47,569 bytes only after content was cut, losing source URLs and release stamps. When `decision_call.py` prints part files, issue every `part_*.sql` VERBATIM one at a time (each <= 24,000 characters, read whole), each returning `staged` or `already_present`, then issue `call.sql`. A part refused for a digest mismatch is re-issued alone; a `call.sql` refused for missing parts names them: issue those part files then re-issue `call.sql`. The same bounded-retry rule applies per file, with the same `research_screen_write_refused` escalation. Any agent, orchestrator or sub-agent, may issue the files. NEVER compact, summarize or drop `fields` content to make a call fit — the split exists so the full screen lands.

   **Strategy-B handoff identity.** For every D1-originated Strategy-B candidate or `research-screen` item, persist the qualifying public-event date as `qualifying_event_date` (not merely a ticker or the D1 run date).

   **ANCHOR CONVENTION — `qualifying_event_date` IS THE DATE THE EVENT BECAME PUBLIC, NEVER THE SESSION THE MOVE WAS MEASURED IN (added 2026-09-21 by D1, closing its own `d1_qualifying_event_date_anchor_unspecified`, `ops.alerts` info `03b8f773`, 2026-09-16).** Apply `Watchlist.md`'s **ANCHOR PIN**: the event date governs; flag-date wording is legacy.
   - **The rule, stated operationally.** Anchor on the date qualifying information CROSSED THE WIRE. An **after-close** release on session S anchors on S, with S+1 as reaction session. An **intraday** or **pre-open** release on S anchors on S, with the ≥5% test measured on S. Record BOTH `qualifying_event_date` (anchor) and the reaction session used for `prior_close`/`event_close`, so the distinction is explicit.
   - **THE ANCHOR AND THE MEASUREMENT ARE TWO CLOCKS — MEASURE CRITERION 1 ON THE REACTION SESSION, ANCHOR THE WINDOW ON THE RELEASE.** This forbids anchoring on reaction session, not measuring ≥5% there. For AFTER-CLOSE releases, S fixes entry-window start and the 10-trading-day count; `metric_pct`, `prior_close`/`event_close` and `below_spec_floor` use S+1, the first session able to price the information. Intraday/pre-open clocks coincide on S. Apply `Weekly_Post_Event_Screen.md`'s convention. The headline's “measures the ≥5% move on event day” means the first session able to price the event, not necessarily the anchor.
   - **WHY THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: THE ANCHOR CAN DECIDE ELIGIBILITY.** Strategy B Entry criterion 1's ≥5% test uses the correct reaction session; moving the tested session can reverse eligibility.
   - **It also silently shortens windows.** The 10-trading-day entry window runs from the anchor; reaction-session anchoring can incorrectly extend it.
   - **Do not resolve the anchor from the price series.** Bars establish reaction session, not publication time. Resolve from the issuer/authority release timestamp required by the EVENT-IDENTITY GATE. If it cannot be established, state this and record the anchor as UNRESOLVED, never default to reaction session. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-04.)*

   A B thesis candidate's deterministic identity is `analysis_type='thesis-construction'` + `strategy='B'` + `ticker` + `qualifying_event_date`, with queue `item_key = thesis-<TICKER>-B-<YYYYMMDD>` (**KEY-FORMAT PIN, corrected 2026-08-23 by W4 — see §C of W4 for the full record; the previously-documented `thesis-B-<ticker>-<qualifying_event_date>` shape has NEVER been written by any routine and matching on it as a literal string returns a false-negative dedupe every time**). Before D1/D2 creates that handoff, check both open and terminal `events.queue_events` history and relevant `events.decision_log` decisions for that exact four-part identity — **match on the FIELDS `(item_type, strategy, ticker, due_date/qualifying_event_date)`, never on the key string**; do not duplicate it, but do not suppress a later distinct event in the same ticker. Carry `qualifying_event_date` and the originating `research-screen` decision id in `d1_actions` and every downstream queue payload. Ticker-only deduplication is prohibited.

4. Sector-level moves — **AI-SIGNIFICANCE SCREEN (Operating_Protocols.md §19, same call).** Layer-1 rail: any GICS sector ≥1% at sector-ETF level, or notable intraday dispersion. Layer-2: judge significance in regime context per §19. Per written-up sector: magnitude, apparent driver, source, significance conviction + reason, `legacy_rule_pass` (sector ≥2%, old record-only bar; `metric_pct` is raw sector-ETF close-to-close move — **regular-session daily bars (`get_price_history`, `outside_rth=false`), never a snapshot; Operating_Protocols.md §19 PRICE BASIS** — **read the `close` array at both ends and log `prior_close`/`event_close` (§19 FIELD / RECORD THE TWO PRICES)**). Dispersion-only surfacing logs `legacy_rule_pass=false`, never NULL. **A commodity or index level quoted as a driver (Brent above all) is the EVENT-session figure, never the prior session's; state both figures with dates and omit an unconfirmed event-session level rather than substitute the prior one.** **THE EVENT-SESSION BRENT FIGURE COMES FROM THE HOUSE SERIES, NOT A WEB SEARCH.** Read `state.signal_marks_curated` `ticker='BZUSD'` for the event session first. If D2a STEP 1d has not landed it, fetch ONE `mcp__FMP__commodity` `commodities-historical-price-eod-light` request for `BZUSD` over prior..event session dates (D2a's source), logging an `ops.web_calls` `provider='fmp'` row. Quote “Brent (BZUSD, provisional same-evening read) <close> on <date>”, with prior close from the same series. This label is mandatory under STEP 1d's VENDOR REVISES THIS SERIES rule: same-evening BZUSD is provisional, never an exchange settle, and a later restatement is not a defect. Web-searched settles are context only, never the quoted level. Only if FMP has no event-session row is the level unavailable: omit it and do NOT raise `brent_event_session_settle_unconfirmed`, the documented handling. Log ONE `entry_type='research-screen'` row (screen='sector-move') per §19, including quiet days. **`surfaced_count` means `ARRAY_LENGTH(passed)`, never Layer-1 rail tally**; use `fields.rail_tally` / `fields.universe_measured` for population arithmetic. Write and correct via the single-name WRITE PATH (`scripts/decision_call.py` → `ops.sp_log_decision_checked`). Apply the same late-data discipline: re-read final state before initial append; after append, emit an append-only complete replacement preserving `entry_type='research-screen'`, tag `correction`, and `in_superseded_by=<old entry_id>`; never events.decision_log UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE. **SECTOR-ETF CONTRACT-ID REGISTRY:** XLK=4215230, XLF=4215220, XLV=4215205, XLY=4215215, XLP=4215210, XLE=4215217, XLI=4215227, XLB=4215200, XLU=4215235, XLRE=209048377, XLC=322317077. **Use these ids directly; do NOT carry ids from memory or a prior run**, because a wrong sector id can still return clean bars. On first use each run, check close is near that ETF's prior-day close in the preceding `research-screen` row; for an absent symbol or suspect bar, re-resolve with `search_contracts` (exact `symbol`, `exchange` ARCA) and log corrected id in item. **INDEX-TAPE CONTRACTS NEED THEIR NATIVE EXCHANGE.** `^VIX` contract_id 13455763 and SPX 416904 are `security_type='IND'`; every `get_price_history` call passes `exchange='CBOE'` per the IND bullet above. Do not raise `ibkr_vix_index_daily_bar_unavailable` without trying CBOE. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-05.)*

5. Notable commentary. Major sell-side reports issued, regulator or central-bank speeches with market-moving content, senior corporate commentary worth noting.

ANALYSIS — RISK TO EXISTING POSITIONS

MECHANICAL EXIT-TRIGGER SWEEP (run for EVERY open position regardless of whether any Development fired). Read the open book + its two MECHANICAL exit triggers (`convergence_target`, `time_exit_date`, with `contract_id`) from **`state.current_positions`** (BigQuery — authoritative per Operating_Protocols.md §15, D2-maintained), and pull live prices from the IBKR connector (`get_price_snapshot` per name). **Sweep the UNION of `state.current_positions` and live `get_account_positions` (self-improvement audit ITEM 14, 2026-07-11 — closes the exact gap that left the BURL convergence exit unactioned for days: a position real in IBKR but not yet reconciled into BigQuery was previously EXEMPT from this sweep entirely, since it enumerated from `state.current_positions` alone and used the connector only for a "flag divergence" side-note).** For a position present in the connector but NOT yet in `state.current_positions`: run its convergence-target / time-exit checks anyway using connector-supplied fields (ticker, average cost, live mark) — its entry record's `convergence_target`/`time_exit_date` are unavailable pre-reconciliation, so treat it as a **RECONCILIATION-LAG POSITION** requiring a same-day D2a Step-0 catch-up rather than skipping its exit check silently. Write a durable `ops.alerts` row — not prose — for every such position: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','position_reconciliation_lag', <ticker + strategy-if-known + first-seen-in-connector date>, <JSON: including ticker, strategy>)` (switched from `sp_raise_alert` to the `_once` variant, root-cause fix 2026-07-20 — the message is pinned to the first-seen date so it stays stable for a persisting occurrence, and `_once` dedups on (category, message) against unresolved rows; without it, a position that fails its same-day D2a catch-up — e.g. IBKR down, guard-blocked — would accumulate one duplicate alert row per subsequent D1 run instead of the one open alert every other persisting-condition category in this file gets). This is a genuine gap distinct from the existing `state.position_reconciliation` (B4) drift check, which compares two BigQuery views populated by the SAME write step and is structurally blind to a not-yet-reconciled connector position. For each position in the union, check the two MECHANICAL exit triggers:
- **Convergence target hit** (Strategy B / E price targets): live price at or through the convergence target → flag EXIT TRIGGERED (mechanical — the target IS the exit rule per Strategy.md; no judgment needed).
- **Time-based exit due**: today (America/Denver) ≥ the position's time-based-exit date → flag EXIT TRIGGERED.
This catches a target-hit the next morning without waiting for a per-position scheduled review — the lag that left the BURL convergence exit owed for days under the screenshot workflow. It retires the per-position pulse-check / time-exit / convergence-check calendar events entirely (this daily sweep replaces them). D2 converts every EXIT TRIGGERED flag into a crafted exit order.

PER-STRATEGY KILL-TRIGGER SWEEP (connector-driven; run for EVERY active strategy, alongside the per-position sweep above). Read each strategy's kill/gate state from **`perf.kill_flags`** (BigQuery engine — `drawdown_kill`, `runaway_review`, `m2m_underperf_review`, `evidence_kill` (the live ramp sequential-test kill, `state.strategy_ramp` via bigquery/259; treat exactly like `drawdown_kill`: immediate mechanical termination through the existing handler, no review), and the historical `gate_reached` (the retired 30-trade gate; drives nothing since rev 20), computed from the latest `perf.strategy_daily`). D1 runs before D2, so the engine row is yesterday's close — **UNCONDITIONALLY refresh `current_drawdown` against today's live marks (`get_price_snapshot`) for every open position, every run** (AI_Trading_Foundation.md 3b.3 reserves this decision from AI discretion), then evaluate the flags below against the thresholds in Experiment_Parameters.md "Kill criteria (per-strategy)":
- **Drawdown kill (#1, mechanical / immediate):** if peak-to-trough deployed TWR has dropped ≥50% from the strategy's highest historical value since first trade → flag **STRATEGY TERMINATION — DRAWDOWN**. Rigid and context-independent — no judgment, no review.
- **Runaway-success (#3, pre-gate only):** if deployed TWR has **doubled** AND the strategy has not yet cleared its 30-trade gate → flag **RUNAWAY-SUCCESS REVIEW** (does NOT terminate directly — routes to an m2m-termination review to rule out reward-function exploitation / hidden tail risk).
- **Interim underperformance warning.** `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning` (`deployed_days >= 90 AND excess_vs_sgov <= -15%`, beta-adjusted; `bigquery/03_twr_engine.sql`) is early/advisory protection before the 756-day/36-month mark-to-market trigger. For each active strategy whose latest `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning = TRUE`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','interim_underperf_warning', '<strategy> — deployed >=90 days, beta-adjusted excess vs SGOV <= -15%, no mechanical kill triggers before the 756-day mark-to-market review', '<JSON: strategy, deployed_days, excess_vs_sgov>')` — a WARNING, not a termination trigger (this signal is explicitly early/advisory, not one of the rigid mechanical kill criteria); it does NOT enqueue a review or route to D2 like the two flags above — it exists to feed SL4's monthly QUALITATIVE-EVIDENCE INTAKE and any session second look, well before the 756-day trigger. `sp_raise_alert_once` naturally dedupes a persisting condition to one open alert, so this does not spam daily. HEAL-RESOLUTION: when the latest `perf.kill_flags.interim_underperf_warning` reads FALSE for a strategy that has an OPEN alert of this category, run `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='condition healed — beta-adjusted excess recovered' WHERE category='interim_underperf_warning' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.strategy') = <strategy>` — the same sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve as D2 Step 0's `termination_close_staged`. This category stays ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy` (it is not resolved by the generic `sp_auto_resolve_alerts`; D1 owns it with strategy-level evidence).
- **B open-book pairwise-correlation warning (KL #12 metric-(d), `bigquery/83_correlation_controls.sql`).** `SELECT n_positions, avg_offdiagonal_corr, min_overlap_days FROM analytics.b_pairwise_correlation` (a single self-bootstrapping row — trailing ~63-trading-day daily-return CORR across every pair of open Strategy-B positions). If `avg_offdiagonal_corr > 0.5 AND n_positions >= 2 AND min_overlap_days >= 40` (a genuine, non-noise concentration — thin-history pairs are excluded from the average inside the view itself, and `min_overlap_days` is computed over the SAME >=40-day qualifying pairs, so the `>= 40` term is simply the "mature evidence exists" guard — NULL/no-qualifying-pairs safely fails it), `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','D1','b_pairwise_corr_high', 'Strategy-B open book pairwise avg correlation exceeds 0.50 — KL #12 concentration control; see payload for the correlation, position count and minimum overlap', '<JSON: n_positions, avg_offdiagonal_corr, min_overlap_days>')`. A WARNING only — it does NOT terminate or block staging (correlation-bucket is informational per Rev 35, Watchlist.md), it surfaces the KL #12 diversification concern for the next B-entry sizing/eligibility decision. **THE MESSAGE IS A FIXED STRING, AND MUST STAY ONE.** `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on `WHERE NOT resolved AND category = in_category AND message = in_message` (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`): put changing correlation, position count and overlap only in payload, never the message, or a persisting condition re-mints daily alerts. This is the same message-stability rule used by `probe_funding_stalled` (SL3 STEP 5), `queue_item_stale` (D3 QUEUE HYGIENE) and W5. Inert unless B holds >=2 correlated positions with sufficient overlap.
D2 converts a DRAWDOWN flag into an immediate strategy termination (close all positions + deterministic redistribution) and a RUNAWAY-SUCCESS flag into an enqueued review. (The mark-to-market #4 and foundation-change #2 triggers are detected on slower cadences — M4 monthly and Q3/A1 respectively — not here.) *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D1.md` § H-D1-06.)*

For each open position, does any Development above ALSO trigger a (judgment-laden) thesis-invalidation exit criterion in the position's entry record (per Strategy.md exit rules for the relevant strategy)? For each position affected: position (ticker + strategy), triggering development, whether the invalidation criterion is met (YES with specific criterion / NO with reasoning).

**DIVIDEND NETTING ON A PRICE-LEVEL CRITERION — MANDATORY before you report a price test as met (added 2026-08-23; `ops.alerts` `070cc2f0`, B:MSCI:2026-07-27).** If the criterion names a PRICE LEVEL rather than a fundamental metric, you may not compare it to a raw close. Read `SELECT * FROM state.price_level_criterion_drift WHERE position_key = '<key>'` (`bigquery/197_price_level_criterion_dividend_drift.sql`) and test against `dividend_adjusted_level`, not `price_level`. The level was fixed at entry; the price series drops by every subsequent ex-dividend, so an unadjusted comparison drifts **always in the fire-earlier direction**. Report BOTH numbers and the dividend you netted out. **Two flags on that row are not optional reading:** `marks_cover_reference = FALSE` means `events.daily_marks` does not reach back to the reference date and the dividend total is an INCOMPLETE lower bound — reconcile the uncovered head of the window against FMP `calendar` / `dividends-calendar` (the date-range form works on this plan tier only for ex-dates within ~4 weeks of the call and spans of at most 60 days, per shared FMP silent-failure (iv-b)/(iv-c); the per-symbol `dividends-company` form does not work at all. An older head comes back `ACCESS DENIED`, so take it from the issuer's own declaration and name the source) before concluding; `reference_date_declared = FALSE` means the criterion never recorded WHICH date its level was observed on, so the view fell back to the entry date, which is a lower bound rather than the truth. **The worked instance:** B:MSCI's criterion named the 550.79 post-event trough — the 2026-07-24 CUM-DIVIDEND closing low. MSCI went ex-dividend 2.05 on 2026-08-14. The 2026-08-17 close of 550.68 read as a breach by 0.11 (0.020%) against a line 2.05 (0.372%) too high — the distortion was **18.6x the breach margin**. The like-for-like line is 548.74, and 550.68 sits 1.94 ABOVE it: on a total-return basis the criterion was NOT breached. The position was exited anyway.

For each watchlist candidate: does any Development materially change candidacy status (closer to entry / invalidated / unchanged)?

ANALYSIS — OPPORTUNITY CHECK

For every Development above, evaluate whether it creates a new entry candidate for any roster-active strategy with `review_cadence: reactive` in `strategy/roster.yaml` (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP sisa-graduate-no-signal-path — a roster-derived set, currently A, B, C, E; D is excluded via `review_cadence: long_horizon` since its multi-year horizons rarely turn on single-day developments; a future SISA graduate is picked up automatically once SL5 registers it, per that field's mandatory declaration at SHADOW-register time). Do not limit evaluation to existing watchlist names — names currently unwatchlisted can become candidates, and names currently held in one strategy can incidentally create candidacy in another (with the simultaneous-holding constraints from Strategy.md respected). Examples of signals to surface:
- Significance-judged post-event move (Operating_Protocols.md §19) on a name fitting Strategy B's eligibility → B candidate (10-day entry window) — **ONLY if it also meets B's frozen Entry criterion 1 (≥5% close-to-close on event day, `strategy/04_strategy_b.md` — §19's spec-floor rail: that number now derives from the frozen spec, not from a screen tune).** A significance-judged mover BELOW the spec floor is `below_spec_floor` context / SL1 ideation evidence only — never routed as a B candidate.
- Newly announced qualifying catalyst within 45 days on a name fitting Strategy C's eligibility → C candidate
- Catalyst announcement within 6 months on a name fitting Strategy A's eligibility → A candidate
