KILL-TRIGGER & GATE EVALUATION (per active strategy — the active-strategy set is `state.strategy_roster` where `is_active`, so a graduated newcomer is included automatically once it reaches PROBE; the 30-trade gate + m2m evaluation stay per-strategy over that dynamic member set, rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion; the slower triggers not covered by D1's daily sweep). **Source: `perf.kill_flags` (`gate_reached`, `m2m_underperf_review`) + the `perf.strategy_daily` indices (the engine row; the former ledger Performance block was just a mirror of it, retired).** ADVISORY CONTEXT (never a trigger — settled design, consumption-closure 2026-07-16): also read `analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` and `analytics.excess_forecast_vs_actual` below_band rows plus the most recent `entry_type='forecast-monitor'` `events.decision_log` entry (M5 STEP 5 — previously addressed to this review but never read), and note per gate/kill evaluation whether the forecast trajectory corroborates or contradicts the mechanical reading; this context never changes a threshold and never stages an action off a forecast. Per Experiment_Parameters.md "Kill criteria (per-strategy)" + the success threshold:
   - **~~30-trade gate~~ EVIDENCE KILL (rev 20, 2026-10-19, owner directive — the 30-trade gate is RETIRED, Experiment_Parameters.md rev 20; the gate procedure after this clause is kept as history and is NOT executed):** for each strategy whose `state.strategy_roster.current_state IN ('PROBE','ADOPTED')` AND `perf.kill_flags.evidence_kill = TRUE` (bigquery/259 — the sequential probability ratio test on the declared edge crossed its lower boundary; FALSE for every strategy without `ops.strategy_ramp_params`, i.e. the founding A–E), execute the TERMINATION-CLOSE craft and the deterministic redistribution exactly as the gate-failure branch below describes, with the `events.decision_log` entry `decision='TERMINATE'` citing `cum_llr` and `trades_n` from `state.strategy_ramp`. There is no gate-pass branch and no graduation here: PROBE→ADOPTED is SL3 R2's `adopt-register` handoff to SL5 on `state.strategy_ramp.graduation_ready`. **HISTORICAL GATE TEXT FOLLOWS.** **PRECONDITION FIXED (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP probe-stake-floor-prose-only) — for each strategy whose `state.strategy_roster.current_state = 'PROBE'` AND whose latest `perf.kill_flags.gate_reached = TRUE`**: read the maintained **deployed unit value** and **SGOV index** at the 30-trade mark; nominal excess = `deployed_unit_value ÷ sgov_index − 1`; apply the **post-tax** haircut (short-term cap-gains rate per Experiment_Parameters.md on the realized-gain portion) and **post-inflation** haircut (CPI over the first-trade-to-gate span) → **excess real return**. **WASH-SALE ADJUSTMENT (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP wash-sale-loss-not-in-gate-math) — fold in BEFORE applying the post-tax haircut:** `SELECT SUM(estimated_disallowed_loss) FROM state.wash_sale_exposure WHERE close_strategy = <strategy>` (`bigquery/41_tax_lots.sql` — built specifically because "a disallowed loss reduces the actual post-tax figure below what the naive TWR-minus-tax-rate estimate implies," Experiment_Parameters.md, but nothing had ever read it downstream). A disallowed loss is not currently deductible, so it must be ADDED BACK to the taxable realized-gain base the post-tax haircut applies to (the opposite of subtracting it) before clamping the taxable base at 0 — this makes the post-tax haircut slightly MORE conservative (a strategy with real wash-sale exposure clears the gate on a smaller true after-tax excess than the naive figure suggested), never less. **If < 0% → terminate** — **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK (2026-07-27, `INCIDENT[ref=423ecc02-fdb7-4f47-9445-d8c79d399e8c]`) — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item. This is deliberately restated here rather than left to the gate paragraph alone: the pre-2026-07-27 design enforced the halt by aborting the routine, so the craft sites never needed their own check; now they do. (execute the close + deterministic redistribution per the D2 termination procedure / Experiment_Parameters.md "Strategy termination and capital redistribution"); write the gate post-mortem to `events.decision_log` (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`). **If ≥ 0% → mark the gate CLEARED**: **write an ADOPTED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row (driver_routine='D2')** — plus an `events.regime_events` (`STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, unchanged, still active) update and an `events.decision_log` entry (permission to continue; not a success verdict). **THEN RAISE THE GRADUATION NOTICE (2026-08-04, owner directive "notify me by email on every roster add/drop"): `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','M4','strategy_graduated', '<code> (<name>) CLEARED the 30-trade gate and graduated PROBE -> ADOPTED — real excess after tax and inflation <X.X>%. Now sized as a full roster member.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract; reason = the measured post-tax/post-inflation excess>')`** Raise it only on the CLEARED branch — the `< 0%` branch terminates, and that path already notifies via `termination_close_staged` plus SL5's `strategy_deregistered`. Record the evaluation either way. (Strategy D's gate is expected never to be reached — low turnover; documented and fine.)
   - **Mark-to-market underperformance (#4):** for each strategy whose `perf.strategy_daily` row shows **`deployed_days` ≥ ~756 (≈ 36 months active)**, compute the rolling-12-month deployed-vs-SGOV gap from the `perf.strategy_daily` series — `(deployed_unit_value/sgov_index now) ÷ (deployed_unit_value/sgov_index ~12 months ago) − 1`; if it has trailed SGOV by **≥ 10 percentage points over any rolling 12-month window** (router-deactivation periods already excluded, since the indices only advance on deployed days), enqueue a `PENDING_REVIEW` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`, queue='PENDING_REVIEW'; review_type m2m-termination; the strategy; trigger_context = the measured 36-month-active + rolling-12-month gap; attacker_due_date next trading day; orchestrator_due_date +1; status pending). The Attacker/Orchestrator adjudicate; on TERMINATE they execute termination + redistribution inline. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/M4.md` § H-M4-03.)*

I. PRE-MORTEM OWNER-ASSIGNED CHECK WALK (added 2026-09-01, closing `ops.alerts` `premortem_live_gate_defect` `6c670d35-c44a-416d-b3e6-73209e66fc3f`, raised by AR_orc on `premortem-C-2026-a3` cycle 17). Load `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` per the read-scope clause above and walk every locus in it whose own text assigns **M4** as the executing owner.
   - **DISCOVER THE SET BY READING THE LIVE FILE EVERY CYCLE — NEVER FROM A LIST HELD HERE.** SL2 changes assignments, so a transcribed roster would become stale. **READ THE SENTENCE, NOT THE STRING, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** A literal `Owner: M4` search over-matches and under-matches at once: it hits two revision-history notes and Known Limitation 9's line, which contains the string solely to explain that KL 9 has **no** owner — none of those is an assignment — while the Code-stack health check's assignment carries no `Owner:` label at all ("manually verified by ~~the participant~~ **M4**", reassigned rev 15) and a string search alone would miss it.
   - **EVALUATE EACH LOCUS EXACTLY AS THAT LOCUS WORDS IT** — its own condition, its own threshold, its own consequence. No reinterpretation, no substituted nearby metric, no invented magnitude or consequence verb. Record one of three verdicts per locus: `EVALUATED-CLEAR`, `EVALUATED-FIRED`, or `VACUOUS-NO-ENTRIES`.
   - **WRITE THE RECEIPT EVERY CYCLE, INCLUDING A FULLY VACUOUS ONE.** `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(<today>, 'premortem-indicator-walk', NULL, NULL, 'WALKED', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 'M4 <YYYY-MM> pre-mortem owner-assigned check walk — <n> loci evaluated, <k> fired', '<one line per locus: strategy, section, locus name, verdict, and the count that makes a VACUOUS verdict checkable — C theses and E pairs entered since the previous monthly review>', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(<n> AS loci_found, <k> AS loci_fired, '<full 40-char SHA of strategy/08_pre_mortems.md at walk time>' AS premortem_commit, <the month this walk COVERS, normally DATE_TRUNC(<today>,MONTH) but the backfilled month when closing a prior notice> AS covers_period_start, [<one STRUCT per locus: strategy, section, locus, verdict, evidence>] AS loci)), ['strategy/08_pre_mortems.md'], ['premortem-walk'], NULL, <session>)`. **A VACUOUS CYCLE NEEDS THIS RECEIPT MORE THAN A BUSY ONE, NOT LESS.** The C and E audits both provide that a review at which no new theses or pairs were entered "is recorded as such and is **not** a miss" — which makes the RECORDING the whole obligation precisely when the substance is empty. M5's walk-presence check reads for this row by `entry_type`, so the literal string `premortem-indicator-walk` is load-bearing and must not be varied.
   - **ON A MISS** — a C thesis or E pair entered since the previous cycle whose `events.decision_log` entry lacks the artifact its locus requires: perform that locus's own stated repair (name the thesis or pair in this cycle's receipt as a transmission miss; reconstruct and record the missing artifact against the live position before the next review), then `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','M4','premortem_live_gate_defect','Pre-mortem owner-assigned check walk found at least one entered C thesis or E pair missing the on-record artifact its locus requires. See payload for the cycle, the loci walked, and each named miss.', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(<run_date> AS cycle, <loci walked> AS loci, <named misses> AS misses)))`. **The loci say `sp_raise_alert`; use `sp_raise_alert_once` with the STABLE message above and carry every varying value in the payload.** That category is registered `latching = TRUE` with resolve_rule "NEVER auto-resolves" (`bigquery/158_premortem_live_gate_defect_policy.sql`), and `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on exact `(category, message)` equality — a message varying by cycle or ticker would open a fresh, un-closable row every month. Deviating from the locus's literal call in this one respect is deliberate and strictly safer; nothing else about the check changes.
   - **`warning`, NEVER `critical`.** `state.trading_enabled` ANDs `blocking_criticals = 0`, which counts every unresolved `critical` outside `trading_halted`/`staleness`, so a critical raised here would halt ALL order staging — exits included — over a documentary transmission finding. Strategy E's Size-attack transmission audit states this constraint in its own words and it binds here unchanged.
   - **CLOSE YOUR OWN PRIOR NOTICE — AND BACKFILL THE MONTH IT NAMES, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE CLOSURE REACHABLE.** Before chat output, read `ops.alerts WHERE category = 'premortem_indicator_walk_missing' AND NOT resolved`. For each open row, FIRST re-walk the loci for the month named in `payload.period_start` — the loci are all of the form "for every C thesis / E pair entered since the previous review", and `events.decision_log` is durable and append-only, so that month is fully reconstructable after the fact — then write its receipt exactly as above with `covers_period_start = <that month>`, and only THEN resolve the row, citing that receipt's `entry_id` in `resolved_note`. **This backfill limb is load-bearing, not politeness.** M4 and M5 both fire on the 1st (`0 15` and `0 16` UTC) and M4 is `catchup_safe: false` and on the catch-up executor's never-re-fire list, so the next M4 cycle after any notice is the FOLLOWING month; a receipt stamped with that month is not evidence about the month that was missed, and `ops.alert_policy` forbids closing on one. Without the backfill the row could never be closed by any mechanism — `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` hardcodes six unrelated categories and the cadence auto-age hardcodes its own list, neither of which covers this one — and because `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on unresolved `(category, message)` with a message that is deliberately FIXED, one permanently-open row would silence every later firing and take the detector dark after its first true positive. Evidence, never age; and never close a row by editing the detector.
   - **WHY THIS STEP EXISTS.** M4 executes the existing owner assignments in `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md`.
   - **BOUNDS. THIS STEP DEFINES NO INDICATOR, MOVES NO THRESHOLD, GATES NO ENTRY, STAGES NO ORDER, AND ADOPTS NO UNOWNED TRIGGER.** It executes only what `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` already assigns to M4. Section 6 bullets that name no owner are DELIBERATELY out of scope and must NOT be swept in — that includes Strategy C's hit-rate, take-profit-firing-rate and intraday-drift bullets and its `[At 15 closed trades]` consolidation (which states outright that "KLs 4, 7 and 11 remain UNOWNED"), every Regime-router Section 9 indicator, and every unowned indicator in Strategies A, B, D and the rest of E. Walking those here would originate monitoring obligations no document assigns — exactly what C revs 16 and 17 declined to do ("a trade-count gate has no monthly-cadence executor to inherit, and naming one would originate a monitoring obligation this document states nowhere") and the mirror image of what the §SL2 pin **AN OUT-OF-SECTION ESCALATION MUST NAME A VERIFIED CONSUMER, NEVER AN ASSUMED ONE** forbids. It stages nothing, so the TRADING-ENABLE GATE above does not reach it. If a walked locus proves unexecutable as worded, do NOT reinterpret it and do NOT edit the pre-mortem — that file is GENERATED from `Strategy.md` and Strategy C's and E's segments feed `strategy/roster.yaml`'s `spec_hash` — instead file it per §Observability's **OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS** rule as an `ops.alerts` `info` row (never promoted to `warning` to force delivery, never forced into `PENDING_ANALYSIS`), which W5's SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE drains. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/M4.md` § H-M4-04.)*

DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: deferrals don't chain. Specify trigger and conservative-default fallback for any deferred decision. Enqueue deferred analyses to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`; never the calendar).

CALENDAR MCP USAGE: Claude calls the Calendar MCP directly only for a non-craftable order's manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order` event (D exits in section C; strategy-termination closes in section H; 2026-07-09 — craftable orders rely on IBKR's own notification instead). Time zone per Experiment_Parameters.md.

CHAT OUTPUT:
- Exit order(s) as crafted instructions (tap-to-confirm deep link + `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF` summary) grouped by execution day (or "no order").
- One-line acknowledgment of file edits, `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued, and confirm-order events created.

If no orders, no file changes, no queue entries: "No actions required."

## M5. Deployed-TWR & Macro Forecast — regular routine

Runs monthly, after M4 (Monthly Action Conversion). The forward-looking monitoring overlay: a zero-shot `AI.FORECAST` (BigQuery built-in TimesFM — **no model to train or host**) over the deployed-TWR engine and, once it accrues enough history, the macro series. **Advisory / early-warning ONLY — it never stages an exit, termination, or activation change. Kill/gate triggers fire on REALISED values (`perf.kill_flags`), never on a forecast** (Experiment_Parameters.md kill-criteria discipline). Not deep research; pure BigQuery. DDL + query templates: `bigquery/06_forecast.sql`.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence, BigQuery read + write. Read `perf.strategy_daily` (the deployed-TWR series), `perf.kill_flags`, `events.macro_series`, and the prior run's `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast`. Also read `state.decision_log_current` for STEP 5's walk-presence check (added 2026-09-01). No web research or repo factbase reads required.

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before the dependency gate below, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='M5' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "M5 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or M5's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the forecast, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('M5', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day; self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

STEP 0 — ensure the store + early-warning view exist: idempotently run `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` **and** `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §store + §B). The view reads the table + `perf.strategy_daily`, so it is safe to (re)create even when the table is empty — STEP 1 needs it to exist on the next run.

STEP 1 — FORECAST-VS-ACTUAL early-warning (skip on the first-ever run). Query `analytics.twr_forecast_vs_actual` (the most-recent PRIOR run's `deployed_unit_value` forecast vs realised `perf.strategy_daily` for now-elapsed dates). Flag any strategy whose realised deployed-unit-value landed BELOW the prior forecast's `pi_lower` (downside surprise — possible regime shift / unmodeled deterioration) or above `pi_upper`. This is the calibration + early-warning signal.

Also read `analytics.excess_forecast_vs_actual` (the m2m-proxy series, previously stored-but-never-calibrated) and `analytics.macro_forecast_vs_actual` (last vintage's macro forecasts vs since-published FRED prints; bigquery/77_forecast_consumption.sql), folding notable breaches into the STEP 5 entry. ALERT DISCIPLINE (strategy series only; macro breaches stay decision_log-only): restrict to the MOST RECENT prior vintage — `forecast_run_date = (SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM analytics.deployed_twr_forecast WHERE run_date < CURRENT_DATE("America/Denver"))` — never alert off older vintages. First heal: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note="band breach healed (M5 STEP 1)" WHERE NOT resolved AND source="M5" AND category="forecast_downside_breach"` for each open breach alert whose strategy/series shows no below_band row in the latest vintage (sanctioned in-place resolution — the bigquery/34 lifecycle pattern; ops.alerts is not append-only-watched). Then for each strategy whose realised `deployed_unit_value` OR `excess_vs_sgov` landed below the latest prior vintage's `pi_lower`: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once("warning","M5","forecast_downside_breach","<strategy> — realised <series> below the prior 90% pi_lower (downside surprise; advisory, never a trigger)","<JSON: strategy, series, forecast_run_date, forecast_date, pi_lower, actual>")` so the early warning reaches the monitored email channel (alert_emailer.gs already emails severity=warning). Keep the message string exactly as templated — sp_raise_alert_once dedups on unresolved (category, message).

STEP 2 — NEW deployed-TWR forecast. Run `AI.FORECAST` per active strategy over `perf.strategy_daily`, horizon 21 (~one trading month), `confidence_level => 0.9`, for two series: `deployed_unit_value` (drawdown / profitability path) and `excess_vs_sgov` (relative-perf / mark-to-market path). INSERT every forecast row into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` with `run_date = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')` (bigquery/06_forecast.sql §A — INSERT only rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty, so a newly-activated strategy with too few deployed days is skipped rather than written as NaN). **SKIP A FLAT STRATEGY TOO (added 2026-10-26, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE hosted by OPS2, closing M5's `forecast_flat_strategy_backdated`, alert `20e83cfb-003e-44b8-9e66-b5aa2ba6af98`):** forecast only strategies whose `MAX(as_of)` in `perf.strategy_daily` is `>= state.trading_day_today.last_trading_day`. A roster-active strategy with no deployed capital writes no `perf.strategy_daily` rows, so `AI.FORECAST` projects forward from its LAST deployed day and the 21 rows land on dates already in the past at write time — never calibratable (`twr_forecast_vs_actual` finds 0 elapsed actuals) and misread as a live path by any latest-vintage consumer (measured: Strategy B flat since 2026-08-18, both the 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-02 vintages wrote 42 B rows dated 2026-08-19..09-08). Write no row for it; record `<code>: flat since <MAX(as_of)>, not forecast` in the run note. Already-landed backdated vintages are history and are not deleted. (29 deployed days at 2026-06 is enough to run — AI.FORECAST handles the business-day spacing; intervals are wide now and tighten as history accrues.)

STEP 3 — KILL/GATE TRAJECTORY check (advisory). From the new forecast, note whether the central path or `pi_lower` of `deployed_unit_value` trends toward a kill threshold over the horizon — drawdown-kill `deployed_unit_value / peak_unit_value − 1 ≤ −0.50` (#1), or `excess_vs_sgov ≤ −0.10` (the mark-to-market #4 proxy, which only becomes a live trigger at `deployed_days ≥ 756`). A heads-up for the next M4 gate/kill review — NOT a trigger. Do NOT stage any exit or termination off the forecast.

STEP 4 — MACRO forecast (FRED-backed, un-gated). Run `AI.FORECAST` over `state.macro_fred_latest` (15 FRED-derived monthly regime metrics with deep history — 37–54 months each; St. Louis Fed public CSV, no API key; bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql): `data_col => 'value'`, `timestamp_col => 'ref_month'`, `id_cols => ['metric']`, horizon 3, `confidence_level => 0.8`. INSERT the rows whose `ai_forecast_status` is empty into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (`series` = metric, `entity` = 'macro'). The ≥8-obs gate is satisfied for all seeded metrics — keep it only as a guard for any thin/new metric (skip + record `insufficient history (n=<k>)`). Advisory only; TimesFM zero-shot short-horizon central paths on policy-driven series (e.g. `fed_funds`) are noisy, so weight the trend + interval over the point. `macro_fred` is refreshed monthly by M1a appending the new prints (bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql §refresh); M5 forecasts off whatever is current. (The M1a-curated `events.macro_series` audit table is separate and not used here.)

**WALK-PRESENCE CHECK — the cheap gate on M4 section I (added 2026-09-01, same landing as that section).** Before writing the STEP 5 entry: `SELECT COUNT(*) AS receipts FROM state.decision_log_current WHERE entry_type = 'premortem-indicator-walk' AND entry_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), MONTH) AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')`. If `receipts = 0`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','M5','premortem_indicator_walk_missing','M4 completed this monthly period without recording a premortem-indicator-walk receipt — the loci strategy/08_pre_mortems.md assigns to M4 were neither evaluated nor recorded as vacuous for the month. See Claude_Task_Plan.md M4 section I and the payload.', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), MONTH) AS period_start, <m4 run_date> AS m4_run_date)))`. **M5 is the right site and the cheapest one:** it is the EARLIEST monthly routine carrying a FATAL dependency gate that already asserts M4 completed (`SL4` carries the identical `sp_assert_deps('SL4', ['M4'], <today>)` gate but fires 30 minutes later at `30 16`, so M5 at `0 16` sees the gap first; the claim is earliest, NOT unique) (`CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('M5', ['M4'], <today>)` above), so "M4 completed but the receipt is absent" is a content gap M5 can see for one query and that nothing else in the fleet can see at all — `state.cadence_watch` detects a missing RUN, never a missing STEP inside a run that completed. Keep the message string EXACTLY as templated (`sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on exact `(category, message)` equality; the varying values stay in the payload) and keep it a `warning`, **never a `critical`** — a critical would enter the `blocking_criticals` term and halt order staging over a missing audit receipt. The category is registered non-latching with an evidence-based resolve rule (`bigquery/207_premortem_indicator_walk_policy.sql`); M4's next cycle closes its own prior notice as part of section I. **This check reads the receipt's PRESENCE only:** it does not re-run the walk, evaluates no indicator, and stays inside M5's advisory-only charter.

STEP 5 — write a brief decision entry via **`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`** (`entry_type='forecast-monitor'`; appends to `events.decision_log` + embeds in one call, per Operating_Protocols §15): per-strategy horizon-end forecast + interval for `deployed_unit_value` and `excess_vs_sgov`; any STEP 1 band breaches; the STEP 3 trajectory note; macro coverage (metrics forecasted vs. gated).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — e.g. "M5 forecast: B duv(21d) 0.999 [0.97,1.02], excess −0.4% [−2.1%,+1.3%]; D duv 0.96 [0.92,1.00]; no prior-band breach; no kill-trajectory flag; macro 0/12 (insufficient history). Wrote 84 forecast rows + 1 decision_log entry."
```

## M1R. Out-of-cycle Regime Re-score — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH` `regime-refresh` item is open). It sits in the MONTHLY group because it re-runs **M1a's OUTPUT 2** — the strategy-blind 5-axis score — not because it fires monthly. Added 2026-09-05 (owner-directed package): the monthly cadence is the only thing that ever re-scored `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`, so a shock structure that de-escalated on the 5th of a month kept an `acute` reading in force until the 1st of the next one, with no mechanism able to notice. D2a's REFRESH REQUEST is the producer (Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session; it replaced two earlier D2a substeps); this routine is the drain.

```
**QUIET-RUN FAST PATH (read this first; a routing summary of the steps below, not a new rule - every step it names keeps its full wording).** STEP 1's gate is empty on most fires, and on that branch this routine writes nothing but its own run log. Do, in order: (1) the shared Observability **Connector pre-flight** - BigQuery only, via `state.trading_day_today`, which also supplies `<today>` (America/Denver) - under the **TRANSIENT-FAILURE WAIT-AND-RETRY** rule; (2) best-effort `CALL ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`; (3) the **Run logging** START call; (4) **STEP 1 - THE GATE** query exactly as written below. If it returns ZERO rows the fire is QUIET: do NOT read STEP 1b, STEP 2, STEP 2a, STEP 3, STEP 4 or the NON-GOALS; score nothing and write nothing else anywhere (STEP 4's legacy `rerisking_limb_fired` resolve runs only on a drain or covered path, never on the gate branch); (5) the **Run logging** terminal call, status `'completed'`, with STEP 1's real `<note>` ("no open regime-refresh item; standing monthly FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS snapshot of <YYYY-MM> remains in force") - never blank, because `bigquery/147` refuses a blank terminal note and that turns a correct no-op into a `missed_run` CRITICAL; (6) the gate-branch CHAT OUTPUT line, then STOP. The CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT and Read access scope below bind the quiet path in full: `state.trading_day_today` and the gate query are the only reads it needs (do not run `git log`, and do not read any other routine's run notes). Any due row, any ambiguity, or any failure in (1)-(4): leave this fast path and run the full section from the Read access scope paragraph.

Read access scope: daily (queue-driven), and DELIBERATELY NARROW — M1a's blinding rules apply to this routine verbatim, because the output is an M1a-shaped row. Read the refresh queue `events.queue_events` / `state.open_queue_detail` (queue `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH`), prior `events.regime_events` scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` (earlier months' scores, for trend continuity), `events.macro_series` / `events.macro_fred` (the macro substrate M1a already wrote), `state.market_calendar` (trading-day arithmetic for the rubric's windows), `state.signal_marks_curated` with `ticker = '^VIX'` — and ONLY that ticker, the same narrow grant M1a carries and for the same reason — and `state.signal_marks_curated` with `ticker = 'BZUSD'` — and ONLY that ticker (the Brent front-month series `bigquery/217` ingests, read through the CURATED view per `bigquery/216`'s SOURCE TRAP; the shock_overlay grading rubric's baseline/peak/current triplet, its midpoint and its 10-session plateau window are computed from it, and like `^VIX` it is a bare dated index-level series carrying no strategy, position or roster information). For the scoring template read the strategy-blind slice `strategy/09_regime_scoring_strategy_blind_monthly.md` (the `## Regime scoring (strategy-blind, monthly)` section) + `01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md` ONLY; do NOT load `02_regime_router`, `00_preamble`, or any strategy slice. **Never query `state.current_regime` directly** — M1a's blinding rules apply here verbatim (stated above), and that includes this prohibition: the view is `SELECT * FROM events.regime_events` with no scope filter (bigquery/01_schema.sql) and can return `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` rows naming strategies, which this routine must never see (ops.alerts b9629fb8-6c30-4777-84cc-d04d6f6b155a). Use the explicit `scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS'` filter on `events.regime_events`, named above, instead. Also read Experiment_Parameters.md, AI_Trading_Foundation.md. **Public-source event reporting for STEP 2a's `shock_overlay` event sweep, and a cited daily close of a currency against USD where M1a's TWO-SESSION WINDOW rule needs one for a candidate's currency leg or where the grading rubric's FX leg is measured on the scoring date (STEP 2a rule (4)), are ALSO in scope** (added 2026-10-19, interactive owner session triaging the 2026-10-19 alert emails; the FX-leg use added by Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session; review fix): this list is deliberately narrow about INTERNAL surfaces and does not exclude either; both are bare dated public data carrying no strategy, position or roster information, and the FX-leg use reads the same kind of close. STEP 2a gives its tools, its window and the direction it fails in.

CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT — identical to M1a's, and load-bearing here because the trigger for this run came from a routine that is NOT blind. Do NOT read `state.strategy_roster`, `state.current_positions`, `perf.strategy_daily`, `state.current_regime` scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, the unscoped `state.current_regime` view directly (it is `SELECT * FROM events.regime_events` with no scope filter and can return the same `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` rows unfiltered — use the `scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS'` filter named in the Read access scope paragraph above instead; ops.alerts b9629fb8-6c30-4777-84cc-d04d6f6b155a), `state.rerisking_limb_status` (retired by Rev 52, still defined live), `state.shock_price_leg_status` (a mechanical proxy of the rubric's price half, built for a non-blind routine; the triplet this routine records is the one it measures from `BZUSD` itself), any `events.decision_log` / `state.decision_log_current` row with `entry_type` `'fundamental-call'`, `'router-review'`, `'divergence-review'` or `'action-conversion'` (per-strategy activation calls and states; added 2026-10-19, owner decision in an interactive session: wire Strategy.md's daily technical-flip divergence clause literally), or any per-strategy activation rule, and do NOT map axis values onto strategies — that mapping is M1b's job and the activation write is M4's / the router-review machinery's. Do NOT stage, craft, modify or cancel an order, and do NOT touch capital, the roster or `ops.arsenal_control`. The queue item you drain is written strategy-blind precisely so that reading it cannot break this: if the item you find names a strategy, that is a producer defect — score the axes anyway from the permitted sources only, and record the defect per the shared OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule. **THREE READ RULES IN M1a's SECTION BIND THIS ROUTINE BY NAME, not merely through "identical to M1a's" (restated here 2026-09-29, owner decision on alerts `731e53d0-d341-4f44-babd-512e74308ee8` and `cb5143ba-6eaa-43f0-ab3e-297ad768f15d`; this paragraph is hand-written, so an M1a-only rule would leave M1R uncovered — the lesson of `b9629fb8`):** (1) **`ops.run_log`** — select `routine`, `run_date`, `status`, `log_ts` and `session_id` only, never `note`, `error_msg` or `SELECT *`, EXCEPT `note` on this routine's OWN rows with `run_date >= '2026-09-21'`; (2) **`ops.alerts`** — select `alert_id`, `alert_ts`, `severity`, `source`, `category` and `resolved` only, never `message`, `payload` or `resolved_note`, and only for the named predicates `source IN ('M1a','M1R')`, `category = 'rerisking_limb_fired'` (STEP 4's legacy rows) and `category = 'bigquery_quota_exhausted'` — never a board scan, including through a sub-agent; (3) **the shared preamble** — the plan text before the first cadence group names strategies by letter in cross-routine rules; read it for process rules only and carry nothing from it into an axis call. On the write side, never quote or paraphrase another routine's free text into your own note, alert or decision entry — cite by id, category and surface. Full rationale in M1a's Read access scope and CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section; do not restate. Queue-driven, so (per the queue_driven monitoring rule) it is monitored via `state.stalled_runs` + `ops/triggers.json` + `state.queue_driven_silence_watch` + `state.queue_driven_missed_fire_watch`, NOT `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`. `state.queue_driven_missed_fire_watch` (`bigquery/241`) is the per-day missed-slot detector (warning `queue_driven_missed_fire`, one per routine-date); `state.stalled_runs` sees only a run that wrote a `started` row, so a pre-flight halt (no `run_log` row at all) is invisible to it.

STEP 1 — THE GATE, AND IT IS ALSO THE DOUBLE-RUN GUARD. `SELECT item_key, event_id, event_ts, due_date, note FROM state.open_queue_detail WHERE queue = 'PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH' AND item_type = 'regime-refresh' AND due_date <= <today>` (America/Denver, from `state.trading_day_today`). If it returns NOTHING — the common case, since a refresh is queued only on an out-of-cycle trigger — do NOT score anything: log the run `'completed'` with a real `<note>` ("no open regime-refresh item; standing monthly FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS snapshot of <YYYY-MM> remains in force"), write nothing else anywhere, and STOP. A no-op run needs its note MORE than a busy one, and a blank terminal note is refused at write time (`bigquery/147`), which would turn a correct no-op into a `missed_run` CRITICAL. A second fire on a day the item was already drained finds the item `complete`, falls into exactly this branch, and is a no-op — that is why this routine needs no separate SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD.

STEP 1b — WHEN THE GATE FINDS AN OPEN ITEM, ASK WHETHER THE MONTHLY SCORE ALREADY ANSWERS IT, BEFORE STEP 2 (Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session; review fix). An item queued before a monthly M1a run can still be open after it, and re-scoring then would either race M1a or repeat its snapshot. In this order: (i) **DEFER UNTIL M1a HAS SCORED THE MONTH, ON ANY DAY OF THE MONTH.** If `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine = 'M1a' AND status = 'completed' AND run_date >= DATE_TRUNC(<today>, MONTH)` returns 0 (no completed M1a row with `run_date` in the current month), write no `events.regime_events` row and no queue row, leave the item open for the next fire, and log the run `'completed'` with a `<note>` naming the item and the deferral ("M1a has not completed this month's scoring; item <item_key> left open for the next fire"). The deferral holds on every day of the month until M1a completes, not only through the month's first trading day (round-4 review fix, Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session). **Why:** M1a writes its OUTPUT 2 at the month marker `as_of_date` even when it runs late, and `state.current_regime` orders by `as_of_date DESC`. An M1R row written before M1a in the same month carries today's date, later than that marker, so it would shadow M1a's fresher snapshot for M1b and every other reader. Deferring until M1a completes makes that impossible. M1a's schedule is the `monthly first_trading_day` (`ops/cadence.yaml`; its trigger fires on the 1st at 11:00 UTC, two hours before this routine), and its scoring can complete days later. A long deferral is not silent: a still-missing M1a raises its own `period_missed`, and D3's queue-staleness scan stops excusing deferral days after the month's third trading day (`## D3` QUEUE HYGIENE, CLAUSE (e)). That read touches only `routine`, `status` and `run_date` of `ops.run_log`, which read rule (1) of the CRITICAL BLINDING REQUIREMENT above already allows, so it needs no new grant. (ii) **CLOSE AS COVERED WHEN A LATER COMPLETE SNAPSHOT EXISTS.** Otherwise run `SELECT as_of_date, LEAST(MAX(event_ts), TIMESTAMP(as_of_date, 'America/New_York')) AS cut_ts FROM events.regime_events WHERE scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS' AND key IN ('growth_momentum', 'inflation_trend', 'policy_stance', 'risk_sentiment', 'shock_overlay') AND event_ts > TIMESTAMP '<the item's event_ts from STEP 1>' GROUP BY as_of_date HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT key) = 5 AND LEAST(MAX(event_ts), TIMESTAMP(as_of_date, 'America/New_York')) > TIMESTAMP '<the item's event_ts from STEP 1>' ORDER BY as_of_date DESC, cut_ts DESC LIMIT 1`. A row is a complete five-axis snapshot written after the item was queued whose CUT INSTANT (`cut_ts`: the earlier of its last write and the start of its `as_of_date` in America/New_York) is later than the item's `event_ts`; a fallback-suppression-only write carries no axis rows, so it never matches. **Why the cut instant, not the write time (round-4 review fix, Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session):** a snapshot sees data only up to the session before its `as_of_date`, however late it is written. The `as_of_date` 2026-10-01 snapshot was written 2026-10-02 07:31 UTC from data through 2026-09-30, so it cannot answer an item queued on the evening of 2026-10-01; its cut instant is 2026-10-01 04:00 UTC. Then do NOT re-score: skip STEP 2 and STEP 2a, write STEP 3's terminal row with `payload.covered_by_as_of` = that `as_of_date` and `payload.covered_by_snapshot_ts` = that row's `cut_ts`, the cut instant, never `MAX(event_ts)` (review fix, Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session), run STEP 4 with its covered-path note, and log per STEP 5 naming the covering snapshot's `as_of_date`. That snapshot's cut falls after the item was queued, so it answers the request. (iii) Otherwise continue to STEP 2. This adds no retry and no re-queue: a deferred item simply stays open, and D2a stays the sole writer of `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH`.

STEP 2 — RE-SCORE, BLIND, WITH TODAY'S `as_of_date`. Perform M1a's OUTPUT 2 in full: write one `events.regime_events` row per axis (growth_momentum / inflation_trend / policy_stance / risk_sentiment / shock_overlay) PLUS the `_integrative` row, scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`, `as_of_date` = TODAY (never the month marker M1a uses — this snapshot is deliberately dated to the day it was scored, so `state.current_regime`'s latest-wins read picks it up over the monthly row and the seam is visible in the series). Score all five axes, not only the one the trigger was about: a partial re-score would leave four axes carrying an older `as_of_date` than the fifth, and every consumer reads the LATEST row per axis. Values come from the axis enums in `strategy/09` — do not invent a token. Each row's rationale obeys the grading rubric's RATIONALE-RECORDING DUTY: for `shock_overlay` specifically, state (1) the date of the most recent qualifying shock event and of any qualifying resolution event, (2) the pre-shock baseline / peak / current Brent triplet and the midpoint, (3) which legs are ELEVATED or ACTIVE and which are not, and (4) whether the plateau re-base fired, with its window, its median and N, or which half failed (Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session), so the next scorer inherits a dated, measured anchor instead of a bare verdict. The rubric CONSTRAINS judgment, it does not replace it: a score that departs from the rubric's anchors must argue against them, by name, in the same rationale. If the macro substrate needed for an axis is genuinely unavailable, apply M1a's fallback-suppression protocol unchanged (≥2 of the 5 primary input categories missing → write the suppression rationale row and score nothing) — never a partial 5-axis write.

STEP 2a — `shock_overlay` NEEDS A LIVE EVENT SWEEP, RUN BEFORE STEP 2's WRITE: AN INHERITED ANCHOR CANNOT SUPPLY IT, AND AN INCOMPLETE SWEEP HOLDS THE STANDING VALUE WHERE IT COULD CHANGE THE GRADE. This step supplies STEP 2's `shock_overlay` input, so complete it before that write. Under the Rev 52 rubric the event record decides what no price series can: whether the plateau re-base's event half holds (no qualifying event dated within the trailing 10 sessions), whether a qualifying resolution event has closed the shock structure, and whether a qualifying event has opened one or restarted a re-based elevation. `BZUSD` is a price series, not an event record. The prior `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` `shock_overlay` rationale's recorded events speak only for the window that scorer swept. That rationale states the window, and it can end days before the row was written. A lack of recorded events after an inherited anchor is an absence of evidence, never a measured quiet spell, so never use it as one. Rules: (1) SOURCE — sweep for qualifying events and qualifying resolution events as the rubric defines them, dated per M1a's HOW A SHOCK QUALIFYING EVENT IS DATED rule (which binds this routine by name). Use the same public-source research tools M1a uses for that input — `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `tavily_search`, `tavily_extract` — under the shared External-content extraction discipline and the shared "Metered external calls" rule, including its `ops.web_calls` row. FMP's news tool is plan-gated on this tier and is not a sweep source. Public wire and primary-source reporting carries no strategy, position or roster information, so this read sits inside the blinding rules above. Searching by the shock channel the prior `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` rationale names is expected; no strategy name, strategy letter, position or roster detail ever goes into a query. The sweep re-runs no OUTPUT 1 macro ingest (NON-GOALS) and changes nothing about how the other four axes are scored. (2) COVERAGE — the window starts at the EARLIEST session the prior `shock_overlay` rationale recorded as unswept, or at the start of that rationale's own window if its sweep failed completely; where it recorded no unswept session, the window is every completed trading session (`state.market_calendar`) after the last session it states it swept (after that row's `as_of_date` if it states none). It is never fewer than the 10 most recent COMPLETED sessions that make up the plateau window, plus anything reported since the last of them. Re-rule on every event the prior rationale left undetermined (recorded PENDING, or left for the next scoring because unswept sessions left its effect undetermined): treat each as part of this sweep's record and measure it afresh under M1a's rules. This routine fires before the open, so today's session is never one of the 10. The re-base's event half holds only if all 10 sessions were swept and no qualifying event was found in them; a qualifying event dated inside the 10, whether the sweep found it or the inherited anchor carries it, fails that half outright. Which unswept sessions hold the axis depends on the outcome at stake, per (3). (3) FAILURE DIRECTION — symmetric, and narrowed BY OUTCOME to "the event sweep that a leg or a re-base needs", the rubric's own qualifier. If part of the window could not be swept (a tool was unavailable, timed out or returned nothing usable), an unswept session is evidence of nothing in either direction. Keep the axis at its STANDING value, whatever it is, only when something the unswept sessions could contain would change the grade; it never defaults to `acute` and never defaults to lower. (3a) RAISE — a qualifying event the sweep found (E), whose two-session window (M1a's TWO-SESSION WINDOW rule) has closed and meets the criterion, or whose closed sessions meet it on their own, establishes that a structure is OPEN (the axis is no longer `none`) even when sessions BEFORE it went unswept. That carve-out establishes only that a structure is open, never which session anchors it. M1a's ANCHOR CANDIDATES rule (its rubric application, item (e)(1)) binds this routine by name: where an unswept session of this sweep's window before E (and after the re-base where one applies) could hold the structure's first qualifying event, the first qualifying event after a re-base, or a qualifying resolution event that closed the standing structure, evaluate the price leg off every candidate anchor it admits. For a re-based structure that no unswept resolution could have closed, E and the earliest unswept candidate session bound every case: first check whether the maximum `BZUSD` close since the earliest candidate equals the maximum since E, and if it does, proceed off E. From `none`, evaluate E and every candidate session, each with its own pre-shock baseline and its own peak. The FX leg's reference close follows the same ANCHOR CANDIDATES rule: off each candidate's own reference close wherever a candidate could change the structure's first qualifying event, and once, off the recorded event, otherwise. The sovereign-spread leg is read once. If every reading agrees, use it. If they differ, from `latent` or `acute` keep the STANDING value, and from `none` write `latent` unless some leg is ELEVATED or ACTIVE under every reading, in which case write `acute`. Record each candidate anchor and its verdict in the rationale. If an unswept session falls AFTER E, keep the STANDING value, because a qualifying resolution event there could already have closed the structure the event would open. (3b) LOWER — a qualifying resolution event the sweep found, measured the same way, closes its channel's structure. Lowering to `none` still needs every session from the start of the coverage window (2) fixes from the prior rationale (its earliest unswept session, or after its last swept session) to have been swept, because an unswept session could hold a new qualifying event on another channel. Lowering through the price leg still needs all 10 plateau sessions swept wherever the plateau re-base decides the result. (3c) A qualifying event found inside the 10 plateau sessions already fails the re-base's event half outright, per (2), whatever else went unswept. Record in the rationale which sessions went unswept and why, every qualifying event or qualifying resolution event the partial sweep found, and for each whether it moved the grade under (3a) to (3c) or is left for the next scoring to rule on because the unswept sessions leave its effect undetermined; name any hold in STEP 5's note. On its own a hold is one missing input, not a fallback-suppression event: suppression still takes 2 or more of the 5 primary input categories absent, per STEP 2. Otherwise score the other four axes normally and keep the 5-axis write whole. A hold adds no retry and no re-queue: STEP 3 still closes the item. (4) The queue item's existence, its `note` and its `payload` show only that a re-score is due. That includes the `measured_trigger` / `trigger_run_start` pairs, whose names and dates a non-blind routine chose. They are evidence for no axis, no leg and no event, even where the `note` describes a condition or the `payload` names a date. Do not read the `payload` for scoring. Re-measure the price leg and the plateau window from `BZUSD` in this run. Re-measure the FX leg on the scoring date the same way, from cited daily closes against USD (the Read access scope grant), applying M1a's THE FX LEG IS READ ON THE SCORING DATE AGAINST THE STRUCTURE'S REFERENCE CLOSE rule, which binds this routine by name, and never inherit it from the prior rationale. The sovereign-spread leg is read exactly as M1a reads it; this routine carries no separate gauge for it. Take the event record only from this sweep, which includes the undetermined events rule (2) carries forward for re-ruling. This changes no rubric threshold, window or grade; it fixes where the event evidence comes from and which way an unevaluable input falls. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/M1R.md` § H-M1R-01.)*

STEP 3 — CLOSE THE DRAINED `PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH` ITEM. Insert a `queue_events` row (same `item_key`) with status = `'complete'`, carrying the new `as_of_date` and the five scored values in `payload`; on STEP 1b's covered path it carries, instead, `payload.covered_by_as_of` = the covering snapshot's `as_of_date` and `payload.covered_by_snapshot_ts` = the cut instant STEP 1b's query returned (`cut_ts`, never the snapshot's `MAX(event_ts)`), written as `CAST(cut_ts AS STRING)` (for example `'2026-10-01 04:00:00+00'` for the `as_of_date` 2026-10-01 snapshot, which reads back as the same TIMESTAMP), and still closes the item. D2a's REFRESH REQUEST reads that close as a refresh made at the cut instant, so it answers only requests made before it: the snapshot saw data only up to the session before its `as_of_date`. Do this in the SAME run as the write in STEP 2 (or as STEP 1b's covered finding), and only after it: an open item is what D2a's REFRESH REQUEST reads as a request already made, so an item left open suppresses every future refresh forever, and an item closed before the score is written loses the request outright if the run then dies.

STEP 4 — RESOLVE ANY LEGACY `rerisking_limb_fired` ALERT, BY `alert_id` (kept by Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session: D2a no longer raises this category, but a row raised before Rev 52 can still be open, and this step stays its only closure path). `SELECT alert_id FROM ops.alerts WHERE category = 'rerisking_limb_fired' AND NOT resolved`, then for each row `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'out-of-cycle re-score completed; item <item_key> drained' WHERE alert_id = '<the id>'` (on STEP 1b's covered path the note reads `'refresh covered by FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS snapshot <covered_by_as_of>; item <item_key> closed'`, since that snapshot is also an actual re-score; on its deferral path this step does not run) — the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve, keyed strictly on `alert_id` and never on `category` alone. This is the closure path that keeps `rerisking_limb_fired` off the permanently-red-advisory list: D2a raised it until Rev 52, this routine clears it, and the category stays ABSENT from `ops.alert_policy` (no auto-age — the condition is only ever discharged by an actual re-score).

STEP 5 — LOG THE RUN per the shared Observability template, with a `<note>` naming the drained `item_key`, the prior and new value of every axis that MOVED, and an explicit "no axis moved" when none did. On STEP 1b's covered path the note names the item and the covering snapshot's `as_of_date` instead, and on its deferral path it names the item left open. A re-score that reproduces the standing snapshot is a real, informative result — it is the rubric's measurement reproducing the standing grade — and must not be logged as though nothing happened.

**NON-GOALS — what this routine deliberately does NOT do, and must never grow into.** It does NOT decide any strategy's activation: D2's item 4 picks up the new `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` row on the SAME evening (M1R fires 07:00 MT, D2 at 17:15 MT) and queues the affected router review(s), and the activation WRITE stays with the existing review machinery — no new writer is introduced anywhere in this package. It does NOT re-run M1a's OUTPUT 1 macro ingest (M1a owns `events.macro_series` / `events.macro_fred`; this routine only READS that substrate, and a month with no ingest yet is a reason to lean on the prior month's prints, not to backfill them here). It does NOT produce `Monthly_Fundamental.md` (M1b's artifact) and does not trigger M1b. It does NOT evaluate any refresh trigger itself — non-blind routines do that, and this routine never reads `state.shock_price_leg_status` or the retired `state.rerisking_limb_status`, either of which would hand it a verdict it did not measure. It does NOT enqueue its own follow-up work: if the re-score surfaces something outside this run's scope, record it per the shared OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule and move on.

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — the drained `item_key`, the new `as_of_date`, and the axes that moved (e.g. "regime-refresh-20260910 drained; as_of 2026-09-10; shock_overlay acute → latent, 4 axes unchanged"), or "No open regime-refresh item; no re-score." on the gate branch, "regime-refresh-<date> closed; covered by FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS snapshot <as_of_date>; no re-score." on STEP 1b's covered path, and "regime-refresh-<date> left open; M1a has not completed this month's scoring." on its deferral path.
```
