**THE SAME SENTENCE PINS THE FIELD AND THE SURFACE AND LEAVES THE DATE PLANE AS AN ENGLISH WORD — AND AT THIS ROUTINE'S FIRING HOUR THE UNPINNED DEFAULT IS WRONG BY A DAY ON EVERY FIRE (pinned 2026-09-27 by AR_orc's own fire; MEASURED below).** The pin above rewrote the LEFT side of the due scan's date comparison into an exact expression and pinned the surface it is read from; the 2026-09-24 pin below bolted a whole `NOT EXISTS` clause onto the same predicate. **The RIGHT side is still the bare word `today`, and until this fire no sentence in this section said where that date comes from.** That asymmetry IS the finding: the term that is already inside the payload is spelled out to the character, and the one term a session must fetch from OUTSIDE the payload was left as prose. This section anchors the identical plane on its WRITE side and does so by name — Step 4's SL2 bullet pins an enqueued `due_date` to "the NEXT calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today` (America/Denver)" — so the anchor existed in this very section and was simply never carried across to the read.

**AND THE DEFAULT IS NOT MERELY UNSTATED, IT IS UNCONDITIONALLY WRONG HERE.** BigQuery's bare `CURRENT_DATE()` is UTC. `ops/cadence.yaml` puts this routine at `cron_utc: "35 0 * * 1,2,3,4,5"` / `time_local: "18:35"`, an evening-MT slot whose UTC instant has already crossed midnight: Denver is UTC−6 in MDT and UTC−7 in MST, so ANY local time at or after 18:00 falls on the next UTC calendar day, in either offset and under either the current cron or any re-spacing that preserves the 18:35 local slot. That file's own cron-migration comment already places AR_orc explicitly in the set of routines "whose UTC firing hour has already rolled into the NEXT calendar day". **So at the instant this routine fires, `CURRENT_DATE()` is ALWAYS `state.trading_day_today.today + 1` — on 100% of fires, not on a boundary case.** VERIFIED LIVE this fire at 18:39 Denver: `state.trading_day_today.today` = `2026-09-27` while the execution host's UTC clock read `2026-09-28`. Every other date defect in this family needs an unlucky day; this one is reached by the schedule.

**AND THE FLEET ALREADY WROTE THIS EXACT HAZARD DOWN, IN THESE EXACT WORDS, AND THEN BOUND IT TO A LIST THAT MISSES EIGHT OF THE NINE ROUTINES IT DESCRIBES.** The preamble §Calendar MCP usage rule reads: "Whenever a routine needs 'today' to create/delete/filter a dated calendar event **or a queue `due_date`**, use `state.trading_day_today.today`. Do NOT use the assistant-context `currentDate` field (UTC-based; **during evening MT it has already rolled to the next calendar day** …)" — the hazard named precisely — and it closes with "**Binds D2, D2a, D3, W4, M4, Q4, A1, A3.**" **AR_att and AR_orc are absent from that list.** MEASURED 2026-09-27 against `ops/cadence.yaml`: **NINE** routines fire at a Denver slot whose UTC instant has already crossed midnight — AR_att 18:00, AR_orc 18:35, D3 18:45, SL2 19:05, SL5 19:25, SL3 20:00, OPS2 22:15, OPS0 22:30, W5 23:00 — so the parenthetical's "already rolled to the next calendar day" is true at EVERY firing for all nine, and **exactly ONE of the nine, D3, appears in that binding list.** (AR_att and AR_orc are in fact the EARLIEST two of the nine, not the latest — stated because an earlier cut of this paragraph had it backwards, and the corrected fact is the stronger one.) **Narrow it to the routines the rule is actually ABOUT — those whose intake predicate is itself a queue due-date comparison — and the coverage is worse, not better: they are D3, AR_att, AR_orc and SL2, and D3 is the only one of the four that the list binds.** D3 is also the only one that self-anchors, carrying its own top-of-routine `DATE ANCHOR:` paragraph naming `state.trading_day_today` as "the single authoritative America/Denver trading-day source" — and it is the one that earned it, by RUNBOOK §37's 2026-07-04 incident where D3 compared `today` against the stale `due_date` column. **Neither AR_att nor AR_orc has any `DATE ANCHOR` equivalent anywhere in its section, and SL2's read side has none either (RECORDED, not fixed here — see the sibling-exposure paragraph below).**

**AND THE OMISSION IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT — THE INHERITANCE WAS DELIBERATELY ROUTED ELSEWHERE, AND THE PLACE IT WAS ROUTED TO POINTED AT A FILE THAT NEVER DEFINED THE PLANE.** §SL2's PENDING_DRAFT LANE CONTRACT states the routing outright: "`PENDING_ANALYSIS` and `PENDING_REVIEW` each carry one document-wide schema paragraph that every producer inherits automatically (the `state.trading_day_today` due-date rule in the preamble Calendar section; **the review-queue block in the Adversarial Review section**)" — so `PENDING_ANALYSIS` inherits the anchored preamble rule and `PENDING_REVIEW` inherits the review-queue schema block INSTEAD. That block is this section's own head, and its `attacker_due_date` field read, from its creation until this fire: "*the next trading day after queue creation, in the experiment's reference timezone per `Experiment_Parameters.md`*". **MEASURED 2026-09-27: `Experiment_Parameters.md` contains ZERO occurrences of `timezone`, `time zone`, `America/Denver` or `America/New_York`.** The lane's single inherited anchor was a dangling cross-reference, which is why no site downstream of it ever had a plane to restate — a broken inheritance chain, not a forgotten sentence. **That head field is corrected in the same commit as this pin** (one line, in the block this routine itself inherits) to name `state.trading_day_today.next_trading_day` and the `bigquery/20_user_prefs.sql` plane directly; it is deliberately the only edit this fire makes outside its own step text.

**MEASURED 2026-09-27, AND THE ANCHOR FLIPS THE SELECTION DECISION ON 88% OF EVERY HANDOFF THIS LANE HAS EVER PRODUCED.** Both anchors evaluated at this routine's own slot on the Denver evening each handoff was written (Denver `today` = D, UTC `CURRENT_DATE()` = D+1), across all **59** `attacker-complete` `PENDING_REVIEW` rows ever written: the Denver anchor selects **4** that evening, the UTC anchor selects **56**, and the two disagree on **52 of 59 — 88.1%**, every disagreement in the EARLY direction. The mechanism is the lane's normal shape rather than a tail: `orchestrator_due_date` is the Denver day immediately AFTER the `attacker-complete` row on **52 of 59** handoffs (same Denver day 0, already past 4, further out 3), because every enqueue rule in this section sets `attacker_due_date` = next trading day and `orchestrator_due_date` = one trading day after that. **A UTC-anchored fire therefore grades the handoff 35 minutes after AR_att wrote it, on the attacker's own evening**, collapsing to ZERO the one-trading-day separation the due-date PAIR exists to create — the same harm the 2026-09-20 pin argued at length ("Early means a column-reading fire selects an entry BEFORE its orchestrator day and grades it") and the same act the RESIDUAL SWEEP below forbids itself on discovery.

**AND NO EXISTING INTAKE GUARD CAN SEE IT.** The RESIDUAL SWEEP tests whether `payload.orchestrator_due_date` PARSES — on all 59 rows it parses cleanly, and the sweep compares it to nothing. The 2026-09-24 exclusion tests whether the cycle already carries a current orchestrator transcript — on an early grab it does not. `state.open_queue_detail` cannot help either: VERIFIED against its live body (`bigquery/01_schema.sql`), that view filters on latest-row-per-`(queue, item_key)` and terminal `status` ONLY, and contains no date expression and no timezone literal at all, so the plane of `today` is left entirely to the calling routine's own SQL. And the 2026-09-20 remedy is no help by construction: it aligned the due scan and the sweep on the FIELD, and both halves now read the identical left-hand expression, while the comparison neither of them makes is the one that is wrong. That is three defects found in this one sentence in eight days, each one term over from the last — surface, field, and now anchor.

**THE PLANE ITSELF IS NOT NEW: IT WAS PINNED TEN DAYS AGO, IN THE SIBLING SECTION, AT A SITE WHERE BEING WRONG COST A FOOTNOTE.** AR_att's 2026-09-17 `STATE THE PLANE, AND USE THE DENVER ONE` paragraph states the premise this rule needs, outright: "*the `today` a fire computes its gap against comes from `state.trading_day_today`, and every `due_date`, `attacker_due_date` and `orchestrator_due_date` in this lane is keyed to the pinned `America/Denver` OPERATING plane*". But it states it about a QUIET-DAY GAP DISTRIBUTION — a figure quoted in a note — and it states it in AR_att's section. So the lane has known the plane, and written it down correctly, for ten days, while the one site where the plane decides whether a review is graded today or tomorrow still said `today`. This is this section's standing defect class in its purest form yet: **a rule stated anywhere other than the site that executes it is not a rule** — and here the rule was not merely mis-sited within a section, it was correct, measured, and parked one section away.

**STRUCTURAL, NEVER REALISED — and a later session must not inflate this into a realised early grading.** Joining every `attacker-complete` row to its own cycle's current orchestrator transcript: **0 cycles were graded before their `orchestrator_due_date`.** That zero is robust to the date basis, which is worth recording because two honest measurements of "graded on time" agree on nothing else: on the transcript's `review_date` COLUMN the split is 45 on-date / 12 after / **0 early** / 2 never-graded, reproducing the 2026-09-20 pin's figure exactly; on the transcript row's own `event_ts` in Denver it is 33 / 24 / **0** / 2. Correct behaviour that is unforced is exactly what this section pins, because the next session may reach for `CURRENT_DATE()` instead and, until this fire, nothing would have stopped it.

**THE RULE: read the due scan's `today` as `state.trading_day_today.today` — the same Denver date this fire logged as its `run_date` — and never as a bare `CURRENT_DATE()`, on any surface.** Stated above at the site that executes it. It binds the two WRITE sites in this section that still name a date only in words, by the same anchor and for the same reason: STEP 0.5's and Step 3.5's re-enqueues ("`attacker_due_date` = next trading day, `orchestrator_due_date` = one trading day after that") mean `state.trading_day_today.next_trading_day` and the trading day after it, never a session-local or UTC clock — which is what Step 4's SL2 bullet already spells out in full for its own `due_date` and what this section's head field now says for the schema. **Deliberately NO new detector and NO new alert category, and do not re-propose one:** once the anchor is named at the executing site, the only remaining way to read the wrong plane is to disobey an explicit instruction, which is prompt discipline and not a data condition — the identical disposition the 2026-09-20 pin reached one term over, for the identical reason. A detector would also have nothing to key on: an early grab leaves a well-formed transcript at a legitimate cycle, and after the fact it is indistinguishable from a punctual one — which is also why the 0-early measurement above is the strongest evidence obtainable here, and not merely the absence of a complaint.

**THE ONE STEP 0 BRANCH THAT PARKS A ROW PARKS IT IN THIS ROUTINE'S OWN INTAKE, AND THE DUE SCAN RE-SELECTS IT IN THE SAME FIRE (pinned 2026-09-24 by AR_orc's own fire).** STEP 0's three dispositions are not symmetric on the queue, and only one of them is a park. "Evidence complete" and "Evidence absent AND NON-binding" both END by inserting the `complete` row, which is terminal and drops the entry out of `state.open_queue_detail` before the due scan ever runs. The BINDING branch deliberately does the opposite, and is right to: a half-executed termination must never be replayed, so it raises the `critical` `review_handoff_stuck` and "**leave[s] the entry at `attacker-complete`**". **That is precisely the status the due scan selects on, and the date term cannot save it** — a stranded entry's `payload.orchestrator_due_date` is in the past by construction, so `<= today` holds on this fire and on every later one. STEP 0's own text anticipates the entry being "re-detected … on each fire until a human clears it" and means re-detected *by STEP 0*; nothing anywhere told the due scan, a dozen paragraphs down, not to pick the same row up again seconds later. This is the section's standing defect class — *a rule stated anywhere other than the site that executes it is not a rule* — in its inverse form: the rule was not merely mis-sited, it was never written at the one site that needed it, because the branch that creates the condition and the scan that consumes it were reasoned about separately.

**AND THE RE-SELECTION IS NOT MERELY WASTEFUL — IT ABORTS THE FIRE.** The re-selected entry runs Step 1 (its current attacker row exists, so the exactly-one check passes), Step 1.5 (equal SHAs, the overwhelmingly common branch), and Step 2 — a full independent assessment, the expensive part — and then dies at Step 3. **VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-24 against the DEPLOYED body of `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`, which is byte-identical to `bigquery/146_adversarial_review_writer_serialization.sql` (SHA-256 `3fa3b773…` over the procedure body, BigQuery stripping only the trailing statement terminator):** inside `BEGIN TRANSACTION` (:106) the write hits `ASSERT p_cycle_number > COALESCE((SELECT MAX(cycle_number) … WHERE review_id = p_review_id AND role = p_role), 0)` (:120-124) and then `ASSERT NOT EXISTS (… review_id … role … cycle_number …) AS 'an active row already exists for review_id, role, and cycle_number'` (:125-131). A stranded cycle fails the FIRST of those two, not the second — the cycle is equal, not greater. **There is no `EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR` handler anywhere in that procedure** (zero matches, whole file), so the ASSERT is a hard RAISE: the transaction rolls back and the error propagates to the job. STEP 0 already names this guard as "what makes this safe rather than dangerous," and it is — no second transcript, no Step 3.5, no Step 4, no capital move. **But it is a guard against a WRITE, not against a FIRE.** This routine has no instruction to catch it, so the fire dies at Step 3 and logs `failed`.

**WHAT DIES WITH IT IS THE RECOVERY PATH, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS.** The park is designed to wait for a human, and every fire in that waiting period now re-raises the critical (harmlessly deduped by `sp_raise_alert_once`), re-grades the same entry, and aborts again. So for as long as the park stands: **any OTHER due entry behind it is never reached**, because the abort happens inside the first entry's Step 3; and STEP 0.5's cool-off re-adjudication, the RESIDUAL SWEEP's condition-keyed heal and the NOTICE-CLOSE PASS all still execute — every one of them is sited before the first entry is processed, the sweep and the pass sitting between the due SCAN and Step 1 rather than before the scan — but they land in a fire that terminates `failed`, which is exactly the state `state.run_log_content_gaps` and the `routine_run_failed` warning were built to make noisy. The one branch engineered to fail SAFE takes the whole routine down with it. **The direction is still fail-CLOSED on capital, and a later session must not upgrade this:** it is a cost-and-availability defect, not a capital one. No wrong verdict can land, and the `review_handoff_stuck` critical has already halted trading before any of this.

**MEASURED 2026-09-24, AND THE POPULATION IS NOT EXOTIC.** Of the 206 `PENDING_REVIEW` rows ever written, `divergence-review` — one of the three BINDING types this branch governs — accounts for **13 of the lane's 39 items and 13 of the 59 `attacker-complete` handoffs, 22% of everything this routine has ever been handed**, tied with `out-of-table-resolution` (13 items, 13 handoffs) and behind only `pre-mortem` (5 items, 33 handoffs). `m2m-termination` and `strategy-retirement` have **never been enqueued at all** (0 rows each), so the branch's reachability rests entirely on `divergence-review` — and that is a fifth of the lane, not a type the lane has never seen. **STRICTLY LATENT ALL THE SAME, and a later session must not inflate it into a realised abort.** STEP 0's detect join has still never had a left side, and this fire closed the *historical* half of that claim rather than re-quoting the 2026-09-16 pin's: of the **60** orchestrator cycles in `state.adversarial_reviews_current`, **45** have a terminal `PENDING_REVIEW` row written AFTER their transcript — the ordinary Step 3 → Step 5 order — and the **15** that do not are, every one of them, the **audited 2026-08-07 JSON-shape repair batch STEP 0 already names**, identifiable because all 15 transcripts carry one identical `event_ts` while their queue rows had already reached `complete` weeks earlier (2026-06 / 2026-07). A transcript written retroactively onto an already-closed entry is the inverse of a stranding, not an instance of it, and none of the 15 is reachable by either STEP 0 or the due scan, since both read `state.open_queue_detail` and a terminal row is not in it. **A later session re-running this measurement will see those 15 and must not read them as strandings.** On the live plane the lane holds **0** rows at `attacker-complete` and **0** at `pending` today (last handoff 2026-09-08, gap 16 days; last enqueue 2026-09-05, gap 19 days — both comfortably inside the documented 27/6/3/4/5/2/2/6/5/2/1/5-day handoff distribution, so the silence is the lane's norm and is carried as a prior, never as a finding). No fire has yet had anything to re-select, and this pin therefore closes the exposure before its first occurrence, exactly as STEP 0 and the RESIDUAL SWEEP each did.

**THE RULE: the due scan excludes any entry whose cycle already carries a current orchestrator transcript** — the exact negation of STEP 0's detect join, stated above at the site that executes it. It is condition-keyed and re-derived from live state on every fire, so it needs no marker and **cannot be defeated by a dropped payload key**, the defect class Step 5 had to fix for `artifact_moved` and Step 4 for `echo_suspect_cooloff`; and it self-clears the instant a human advances the row, never on age. It is deliberately **WIDER than the branch that motivated it**: a cycle whose transcript is already written has already been graded, and STEP 0 says so outright — "*the written transcript IS the verdict of record for this cycle*" — so no branch of this routine, present or future, has any business re-grading it, and a fix scoped to just the BINDING park would have to be re-derived the next time some other branch leaves a row in place. Use `SAFE_CAST`, not the bare `CAST` STEP 0's detect join carries, so an unparseable `cycle_number` can never turn the exclusion itself into a query error; a NULL cycle then simply fails to match and leaves the entry selectable, which is the status-quo direction and the RESIDUAL SWEEP's concern rather than this clause's. **VERIFIED BY POSITIVE CONTROL 2026-09-24, not merely by a clean run:** the amended due scan executed against live BigQuery returns 0 rows today, as it must with the lane empty — a result a vacuously-true predicate would also produce — so it was re-run against three SYNTHETIC `attacker-complete` rows manufactured from real orchestrator transcripts (`otr-router-shock-override-2026` c1, `premortem-C-2026-a3` c18, and `div-E-202608-1` c2, the last of them a `divergence-review`, i.e. the exact BINDING type this pin governs). All three are selected by the predicate as it stood and **EXCLUDED by the amended one**. The exclusion fires, and it fires on the type that matters. **Deliberately NO new alert category and NO new detector, and do not re-propose one:** the condition this exclusion prevents is created by the loudest raise this routine can make — STEP 0's own `critical` `review_handoff_stuck`, which parks the entry and holds `state.trading_enabled` FALSE until a human clears it — so a second category watching the same park would only duplicate the alert that created it. **And the excluded row is not thereby unwatched — check this before concluding otherwise:** a parked entry is invisible to the due scan by this clause and invisible to the RESIDUAL SWEEP on its own terms (its `orchestrator_due_date` parses cleanly, which is the only thing that sweep tests), so neither half of the intake counts it — but STEP 0 re-detects it on **every** fire, by a predicate that is exactly this exclusion's positive form, re-raises `review_handoff_stuck` under `sp_raise_alert_once`'s unresolved dedup, and gives it its own CHAT OUTPUT line. That is a stricter watch than either intake half offers, so this is not the "counted by nobody" shape the sweep was written to close; it is the one row in this lane whose watcher runs first. **And it changes NO conjunct of the quiet-day line:** an exclusion is a predicate, not an action, so a fire that excludes an entry has nothing to report, and the STEP 0 branch that parked the row already forbids a quiet day and already gets its own CHAT OUTPUT line. Do not add a sixth conjunct for it.

**AND THE SIBLING ROUTINE ALREADY WROTE HALF OF THIS RULE, WHICH IS WHY ITS ABSENCE HERE IS AN OMISSION RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE.** AR_att's STEP 0 — the attacker-side counterpart, added 2026-08-17 out of the same `review_handoff_stuck` incident — states the exclusion in its own text on its repair branch, verbatim: "*An entry repaired here is finished for this fire and is not also processed as a due entry below.*" So the convention this section was missing is not novel and was never disputed; it was simply never carried across when STEP 0 landed here on 2026-08-18, one day later, and nothing noticed because both of AR_orc's non-parking branches advance the row to `complete` and are therefore excluded by status without needing a sentence. **The one branch that does not advance the row is the one branch that needed the sentence, and it is the binding one.**

**SIBLING EXPOSURE — RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE, because it is AR_att's section and not this routine's.** AR_att's own STEP 0 is guarded on its repair branch twice over (it advances the row to `attacker-complete` AND says the sentence above), but its FAILURE branch has the identical unguarded shape this pin closes here: "*If the hash check fails, leave the queue row untouched and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','AR_att','review_handoff_stuck','<item_key> — attacker transcript present but body hash does not match content_sha256; queue NOT advanced', '<JSON>')`*" — the row is left at `pending`, which is exactly the status AR_att's own due scan one paragraph below selects on, and the exclusion sentence sits on the other branch where it cannot reach it. The direction is the same (fail-CLOSED on the write, fail-OPEN on the fire), and AR_att's section carries no pin, measurement or latency note for that branch at all. **RESIDUAL SWEEP — run AFTER the due scan and BEFORE the no-op branch below (added 2026-09-13 by AR_orc's own fire; the ORCHESTRATOR-side counterpart of the residual sweep AR_att added to its own scan step earlier the same evening, and specifically the one seam that sweep cannot cover).** AR_att's sweep counts actionable `PENDING_REVIEW` rows whose status is neither `pending` nor `attacker-complete`, plus any `pending` row with a NULL `due_date`. **By construction it EXCLUDES every `attacker-complete` row — which is exactly this routine's intake.** So an entry at `attacker-complete` whose `orchestrator_due_date` is absent, NULL or unparseable is actionable in `state.open_queue`, is skipped **in silence** by the predicate above (`NULL <= today` evaluates to NULL, i.e. FALSE, and never raises), and is counted by nobody: AR_att drops it on status, AR_orc drops it on the date, and `state.queue_venue_claim_unwired`'s `allowed_drainers ['AR_att','AR_orc']` claim is once again true at LANE granularity and false one level down — the identical shape AR_att found for status, one field over. **DIVERGENCE-REVIEW STANDING-CYCLE PRE-CHECK — for each due `divergence-review` entry, BEFORE Step 1 (added 2026-10-19, owner decision in an interactive session: wire Strategy.md's daily technical-flip divergence clause literally).** A replaced call or vanished daily-flip divergence can close a review without adjudication. This routine, the lane's sanctioned closer and activation writer, is the only place that closes one this way; D2 never does.
   - **Read.** The strategy's standing call: `SELECT strategy, entry_id, event_ts, JSON_VALUE(fields, '$.cycle_as_of') AS cycle_as_of, JSON_VALUE(fields, '$.reconciled_call') AS reconciled_call FROM state.decision_log_current WHERE entry_type = 'fundamental-call' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY strategy ORDER BY JSON_VALUE(fields, '$.cycle_as_of') DESC, event_ts DESC, entry_id DESC) = 1`, with D2's ROUTER EVERY-RUN DUTIES TRANSITIONAL READ, CYCLE-DAY GATE and STATE CLASSES applied exactly as D2 applies them; while that gate is closed for the artifact's cycle, this check closes nothing and the entry goes to Step 1, unless the strategy's standing call is a `d2-router-review` row whose `cycle_as_of` is the artifact cycle (M4 A0's D2 DECIDED FIRST case): M4 will not write over that judged call, so test the entry against it here exactly as with the gate open, and close it SUPERSEDED when it is not IN THE STANDING CYCLE. The review's keys come from D2's REVIEWS ON RECORD query, which takes `fundamental_call_entry_id`, `trigger_class` and `fundamental_call` across ALL the item's rows, because Step 1.5's, Step 3.5's and STEP 0.5's re-enqueue rows need not repeat them; IN THE STANDING CYCLE is D2's definition there, legacy rule included.
   - **SUPERSEDED: the review is not IN THE STANDING CYCLE.** Its call was replaced, and adjudicating it against the artifact would overwrite the newer decision, the measured straddle hazard of a review still open on M1b day. Write no `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` row. Insert the `complete` row into `events.queue_events` (same `item_key`, `queue='PENDING_REVIEW'`, `status='complete'`) with payload `review_id`, `review_type`, `resolution_kind = 'superseded'`, `new_state` = the operative value left in place, and `superseded_by_call` = the standing call's `entry_id` (or `artifact <cycle>` for a transitional one). Log `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type = 'divergence-review'` and `decision = 'SUPERSEDED'`; its `fields` carry the STEP 4 PROVENANCE CONTRACT keys plus `resolution_kind`, with `orchestrator_event_id` NULL because no transcript is written. D2's next run reviews any divergence that remains against the new call and clears the stale ` — PENDING` suffix.
   - **MOOT: the review is IN THE STANDING CYCLE, its `trigger_class` is `'daily-technical-flip'`, and its divergence is gone.** Re-evaluate the strategy's `### Router activation rule` technical line on the latest `TECHNICAL_SIGNAL` rows, with the breadth leg per D2's BREADTH LEG FRESHER THAN ITS SIGNAL; if a key it reads is older than `state.trading_day_today.last_trading_day`, do not close, and go to Step 1. If the line's class equals the class of the review's `fundamental_call` (the standing call, since the review is in its cycle), Strategy.md makes agreement mechanical. Immediately before writing, re-run the Read above: if the standing call changed since this check read it (a D2 run overlapping this fire wrote a `fundamental-call` row), close SUPERSEDED as above instead. Otherwise write `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` with `value` = that class as the bare token (which also removes the held suffix), `as_of_date` = `state.trading_day_today.today` (D2's AS-OF PIN), `divergence_id` = the `item_key`, `source_review_ref = 'AR_orc moot <item_key>'`, and a `rationale` naming the legs. If that changes the class, run D2's FLIP CONSEQUENCES (ROUTER EVERY-RUN DUTIES) in this run. Insert the `complete` row as above with `resolution_kind = 'moot'` and `new_state` = the value written, and log as above with `decision` = the value written plus `technical_call`, `technical_as_of`, `breadth_leg` and `breadth_leg_source`.
   - **A closed entry is finished for this fire.** Run none of Steps 1–5 for it: no assessment, no orchestrator transcript, no theater gate, and no `p_queue_event_id` to consume. **Its notices still close, as they would after an executed verdict:** after the close row, run for this `item_key` and cycle Step 4's ECHO-SUSPECT COOL-OFF RESOLVE (gated on its cycle-scoped `is_cooloff_cycle` alone, since no Step 3.5 runs), Step 4's `echo_suspect_requeue` heal and Step 5's ARTIFACT-DRIFT NOTICE RESOLVE, each `resolved_note` naming this MOOT or SUPERSEDED close in place of an executed verdict: the withheld binding those notices report no longer exists, and STEP 0.5 cannot re-detect a park whose latest row is this close. Neither close is a verdict: D2's test (b) reads `resolution_kind`. AR_att is unchanged and may already have attacked an entry that closes here; that is an accepted cost. Any other entry goes to Step 1 normally, and for a `daily-technical-flip` entry the technical call under review is the one this check just re-read. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/AR_orc.md` § H-AR_orc-04.)*

This exact row is the attacker→orchestrator handoff. Preserve strict blinding: AR_att did not read this row; AR_orc may read only this same-cycle attacker row, not a prior review/cycle. Select `source_commit_sha` on this same row — Step 1.5 needs it and it costs no extra query.
   **NULL-CYCLE RESOLUTION — a `divergence-review` payload may carry NO `cycle_number`; resolve it, never abort on it and never default it (pinned 2026-10-20 by AR_orc's own fire).** Divergence-review payloads can omit the cycle key. **THE RULE:** when `JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number')` IS NULL, take the cycle from the attacker side — the `cycle_number` of the current `role='attacker'` row(s) for this `review_id` in `state.adversarial_reviews_current` — and require **exactly one** such row; zero or several is still the data-integrity failure above. Use that resolved cycle wherever this section says `<queue item cycle_number>` or `payload.cycle_number` for this entry: STEP 0's detect join (as `COALESCE(<payload cycle>, <that attacker cycle>)`), Step 3's write, Step 4's provenance keys and Step 5's close. **Never default to 1:** divergence-review cycles are not per-item (`div-D-202609-1` is cycle 4, `div-A-202608-1` cycle 2), so a constant can name a cycle the attacker never wrote. The producer half is RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE (it is M4's and D2's write surface): `ops.alerts` `info` `divergence_review_payload_missing_cycle_number` (`cc07007b`) names W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE as owner — cite it, do not re-file it.
1.5. **ARTIFACT-VERSION GATE — SYNCHRONOUS, before Step 2 (audit of the 2026-08-07 daily runs).** This gate mechanically requires the same artifact text the attacker read; `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review` records `p_source_commit_sha`.
   - Resolve the artifact's **current** commit: `git log -1 --format=%H -- <artifact_path>`. Compare the full 40-character SHA to the attacker row's `source_commit_sha`. (Compare full SHAs, never abbreviations — `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review` ASSERTs a 40-char SHA-1 or 64-char SHA-256, while queue payloads carry short hashes; comparing a short against a full is a guaranteed false mismatch.)
   - **If they are equal** — the overwhelmingly common case — proceed to Step 2 normally. Record the SHA in the orchestrator transcript's provenance line and say nothing further.
   - **If the attacker row's `source_commit_sha` IS NULL** (an intentionally uncommitted snapshot, per the column's own contract): proceed, but state in the transcript that the pair could not be version-matched and treat the theater-check with the same skepticism a MIXED flag earns. A NULL is a known, declared gap, not a drift. **Check this BEFORE the two branches below** — a NULL is not comparable, so it must never fall through to them as a "difference" (ordering pinned 2026-08-19, when the section-scoped fallback was inserted).
   - **If they differ, run the SECTION-SCOPED FALLBACK before withholding (added 2026-08-19 by AR_orc's own first live firing of this gate; it withheld a review whose text provably had not changed).** The file-SHA above is a fast path, not the question the gate actually asks. The question is whether the pair read the same TEXT, and **`strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` is a SHARED artifact: all five pre-mortem reviews (A, B, C, D, E) name it as their `artifact_path`.** SL2 revises it whenever any one strategy's pre-mortem is redrafted, and often revises several at once — so under a file-level comparison, ANY revision to ANY section withholds EVERY other in-flight review of that file. That is not a rare nuisance, it is a **livelock**: the withheld review is re-enqueued, its next cycle lands inside the window of the next revision to some other strategy's section, and it is withheld again, indefinitely, with the cycle counter climbing and zero information produced per cycle.
     - Extract **the section under review** at BOTH commits (`git show <sha>:<artifact_path>`) and compare their SHA-256. The section is the region the queue entry scopes to: for `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` that is the entry's `strategy` code's heading — `### Pre-mortem: Strategy <code>` through the next `### ` heading or EOF. For an artifact under review as a whole, the "section" is the whole file, so this fallback degenerates to the file comparison and changes nothing.
     - **Section hashes EQUAL → the pair demonstrably read the same text. PROCEED to Step 2.** Record BOTH facts in the orchestrator transcript's provenance line — the file moved, the section did not, with both hashes and the intervening commits — so the version match is auditable rather than assumed. Do not raise the drift alert and do not re-enqueue.
     - **Section hashes DIFFER, or the section cannot be located deterministically at both commits → fall through to the withhold branch below, unchanged.** An ambiguous or unlocatable section is a DIFFER, never a pass: this fallback may only ever narrow a withhold on positive byte-identity evidence.
     - This is strictly narrower than "file differs → withhold" and strictly stronger than "file equal → proceed": it can never admit a section that changed. It is still wholly mechanical — two `git show` calls and a hash compare, no judgment, no re-reading of the artifact's meaning, and no re-attack.
   - **If they DIFFER and the section-scoped fallback above did not clear it:** WITHHOLD the verdict for this cycle. The attacker's critique is not evidence about the current text and must not be graded as if it were. Do NOT re-attack the artifact yourself — that would collapse the attacker/orchestrator separation this routine exists to preserve. Instead, mechanically:
     - Re-enqueue a fresh attacker cycle of the SAME review: `INSERT INTO events.queue_events` (same `item_key`/id, `queue='PENDING_REVIEW'`, `status='pending'`, `review_type` unchanged, `cycle_number` = this cycle + 1, fresh `attacker_due_date` = next trading day, `orchestrator_due_date` = one trading day after that, `payload.artifact_moved='true'`, `payload.attacked_commit` = the attacker row's `source_commit_sha`, `payload.current_commit` = the resolved head commit). The re-enqueued cycle carries **no penalty and no cap consumption** — the artifact moved under the pair, which is nobody's defect, so this requeue is explicitly EXEMPT from the rev-15 cycle-5 soft cap's forcing question and from the Step 3.5 echo-suspect lifetime cap. Say so in the decision-log entry, or a future cycle-count read will mistake churn for an unresolvable review.
     - Write `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='artifact-version-drift'`) naming the review id, both commits, and the intervening commits touching `artifact_path`.
     - `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','AR_orc','artifact_version_drift', '<review id> — verdict withheld, attacker read <short sha>, artifact now at <short sha>, cycle <n+1> re-enqueued', '<JSON>')`.
     - **THIS NOTICE IS CLOSED BY A LATER CYCLE — the operative instruction lives at Step 5, NOT here (rewritten 2026-08-19, later the same evening; see the note below).** `artifact_version_drift` is registered **non-latching** in `ops.alert_policy` (`bigquery/187`, 2026-08-19), which SANCTIONS the routine-owned resolve but does not perform it: `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts`'s rules are each hardcoded to a different category and reach this one never, so nothing mechanical anywhere will clear this row — the same disposition `queue_item_stale`, `queue_venue_claim_unwired` and `upstream_marker_mismatch` carry. Left unclosed it accumulates one permanent open warning per drift forever. The close therefore happens at **Step 5 of the cycle that DOES produce a verdict for this review id**, keyed off the `payload.artifact_moved='true'` marker the re-enqueue above writes — go read that step for the exact statement. **The close belongs at the site that executes it.** Do not move it back.
     - Do NOT perform ANY of Step 4's actions for this cycle: the prior binding state stays exactly as it was before this review started, identically to the Step 3.5 withhold.
     - **A WITHHELD CYCLE ENDS HERE for this entry (pinned 2026-08-19, later the same evening — that night's live firing did exactly this, correctly, but from inference rather than instruction).** Do not run Step 2, Step 3 or Step 5 for it: there is no verdict to assess, no orchestrator transcript to write, and **no `complete` `queue_events` row to insert** — the fresh `pending` row enqueued above is the same `item_key` and supersedes the `attacker-complete` row under `state.open_queue`'s latest-status-per-item rule, so the entry stays correctly actionable rather than being closed on a cycle that produced nothing. Move to the next due entry.
   Never a chat question, either branch.
2. Produce explicit independent assessment documenting:
   (a) For each weakness the attacker identified, validity assessment (valid Tier 1 / valid but Tier 2-3 / invalid) — for pre-mortem / strategy-adoption; for other types, equivalent grading per the type's protocol. **MECHANICAL TIER TRIAGE (rev 2026-07-10 — Strategy Arsenal autonomy conversion, owner directive).** Tier assignment is done HERE by this orchestrator, mechanically, using the rev-15 working definitions (Tier 1 structural = MUST resolve / Tier 2 calibration = SHOULD / Tier 3 completeness = MAY), logged to `events.decision_log` as part of the cycle outcome, and is deliberately NOT itself re-reviewed (no infinite regress). This absorbs the former "participant with Claude assistance" triage step (Experiment_Parameters.md rev-15) — the human is removed; triage is now fully autonomous.
   (b) Theater in the attacker's output (generic-sounding objections without specific anchors).
   (c) Weaknesses the attacker missed.
   (d) Final verdict per review_type:
       - pre-mortem: SUFFICIENT or TIER 1 DEFECT — REVISION REQUIRED. If REVISION REQUIRED, identify whether to invoke the rev 15 forcing question and answer it in writing per Experiment_Parameters.md (a/b/c). For cycle 5+, justify continuation per the soft cap. **ROUTER AMENDMENT REVIEW (`payload.strategy='router'`; added 2026-10-19, owner directive in an interactive session): a finding that any Shock Transmission Register row's class, exemption or gate should change — B's BINDS row included — IS a Tier 1 defect and grades REVISION REQUIRED, never SUFFICIENT-with-notes. The review exists to decide exactly that, and Step 4's router clause is the only path that delivers the recommendation to the owner.**
       - divergence-review: final activation state for the strategy (ACTIVATE / DO-NOT-ACTIVATE) with reasoning. Apply the default-on-ambiguity rule and the theater-check tiebreaker: if theater_check = CONVERGENT, default to DO-NOT-ACTIVATE regardless of the verdict.
       - m2m-termination: TERMINATE / CONTINUE with reasoning. Default-on-ambiguity = TERMINATE.
       - scope-widening-adjudication: re-widening AUTHORIZED / NOT AUTHORIZED with reasoning. Apply the four-screen test and the CONVERGENT-theater-check requirement per Strategy.md.
       - strategy-adoption: SUFFICIENT or TIER 1 DEFECT — REVISION REQUIRED, with the same rev-15 forcing-question + cycle-5 soft-cap discipline as pre-mortem. Default-on-ambiguity = REVISION REQUIRED (the review's conservative_default is REJECT).
       - strategy-retirement: RETIRE / KEEP. Default-on-ambiguity = KEEP (affirmative RETIRE required); a strategy at the `state.arsenal_rails.n_min` floor is never retired.
       - out-of-table-resolution: RESOLVE / HOLD. Default = HOLD current state/value unless the objective criteria in trigger_context clearly resolve it (no attack was performed — non-adversarial triage). **WHERE `trigger_context` IS ABSENT, READ `payload.resolves_when` PLUS THE QUEUE ROW'S `note` AS THE `trigger_context` OF RECORD — AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT AN ABSENT CRITERION (added 2026-09-21, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing AR_orc's `otr_payload_missing_trigger_context`, alert `f603c8a9-ba30-4165-8b0a-39956b614a0f`).** HOLD remains the default on genuine ambiguity; what is forbidden is reaching it merely because one key name was missing.
       - prose-regression: CONFIRMED DRIFT / FALSE POSITIVE. Default-on-ambiguity = FALSE POSITIVE (no attack performed — non-adversarial triage; this is a record-keeping mechanism, not a gate, so ambiguity should not manufacture a finding).
   (e) Theater-check flag: CONVERGENT / DIVERGENT / MIXED with specific rationale referencing concrete claims in the attacker output and the orchestrator's own assessment. The orchestrator self-certifies this flag — accepted-risk note: this is structurally weaker than a separate Theater Auditor routine; if empirical theater-check rates suggest under-detection of CONVERGENT framing, a separate auditor routine can be added in a future revision. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/AR_orc.md` § H-AR_orc-05.)*

3. Append orchestrator output through `CALL ops.sp_write_adversarial_review(...)` as the sole durable orchestrator transcript; **do not create `Adversarial_Review_<id>_orchestrator.md` or any other tracked transcript file.** Format: header (id, review_type, date, cycle_number), final verdict (one-line + binding decision), theater-check flag (one-line), reasoning sections per (a)-(d) above, action taken (if any). Supply all fields from this queue item; `p_role='orchestrator'`, `p_expected_sha256=<lowercase SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 body>`, `p_queue_event_id=<the consumed attacker-complete queue-event id>` — **this is the `event_id` of the `attacker-complete` `events.queue_events` row ITSELF, and specifically NOT the `consumed_queue_event_id` the attacker's own payload carries, which by the join rule stated at §AR_att above names the `pending` row AR_att consumed (38 of 38 attacker rows). The role asymmetry is real and was already documented on the ATTACKER side only; pinned here 2026-08-27 by AR_orc's own fire, which passed the payload key and was correctly rejected by `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s role-specific transition ASSERT. That rejection is fail-CLOSED and cost only a job, but the wrong id is the more visible of the two candidates — it sits in the queue payload this routine is already reading, under a name that reads like exactly what this argument asks for — and the ASSERT's message names the constraint without naming the row to use. Resolve it explicitly: `SELECT event_id FROM events.queue_events WHERE queue='PENDING_REVIEW' AND item_key=<review id> AND LOWER(status)='attacker-complete' AND CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64)=<this cycle_number>`** — `p_source_commit_sha=<the artifact's Git commit, or NULL only for an intentionally uncommitted snapshot>`, and `p_superseded_by=NULL` for a normal write. Retain the returned `event_id`, then perform the mandatory exact-row hash/readback check specified in the shared preamble. Do not continue to Step 3.5 or log completion until it matches; append a verified correction row through the same procedure if it does not.
   **`LOWER(status)`, never a bare `status`, in that resolution query (pinned 2026-09-14 by AR_orc's own fire).** The 2026-09-13 case-normalization named exactly two sites — "here and at STEP 0's detect join" — and this lookup was neither, leaving it the routine's last case-SENSITIVE status read. The omission is worse than no normalization at all, because it splits SELECT from WRITE: the due scan now matches a case-drifted `attacker-complete` row, Steps 1 / 1.5 / 2 grade it at full model cost, and then this lookup returns zero rows — so there is no `p_queue_event_id` to pass, `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s role-specific transition ASSERT rejects the write, and the entry is re-selected and re-graded identically on every subsequent fire with nothing ever advancing. Fail-CLOSED, so no wrong transcript can land — but a permanent no-progress loop that bills a full grading per fire, where before the 2026-09-13 widening the same row was simply never selected at all. **MEASURED 2026-09-14: all 59 `attacker-complete` rows ever written are exactly lowercase, so this is STRUCTURAL, not a realized stranding — a later session must not inflate it into one.** It is pinned anyway because the 4 `OPEN` rows the 2026-09-13 note cites are proof that agent-written status has already drifted case in THIS lane, and a widened SELECT over an un-widened write-side lookup is the one combination that turns a silently-skipped row into a looping one.

3.5. **THEATER-INDEPENDENCE GATE — SYNCHRONOUS, before Step 4 — for `review_type` IN (`divergence-review`, `m2m-termination`, `strategy-retirement`) ONLY (self-improvement audit 2026-07-15, CONFIRMED GAP theater-quarantine-no-unwind).** These three review types write BINDING, immediately-effective outputs the moment Step 4 runs (a divergence-review verdict writes the binding `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` row directly; an m2m-termination TERMINATE verdict immediately crafts close orders and redistributes capital; a strategy-retirement RETIRE verdict routes straight to the D2 termination handler) — unlike `strategy-adoption`, whose independence gate already runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside SL5 before SHADOW registration (see SL5's own step). The independence check must precede binding actions.
   - Best-effort `CALL ops.sp_score_theater()` (`bigquery/11_theater_judge.sql`) — both this review's attacker AND orchestrator rows now exist in `events.adversarial_reviews` (Step 3 just wrote the orchestrator row), so the judge can score it immediately. Wrap best-effort (Gemini/Vertex is a SPOF, same dependency as the ticker backfill) — on failure, treat as UNSCORED (see below), never abort the routine.
   - Read `SELECT judge_independent FROM analytics.theater_judge WHERE review_id = <this review's id>`.
   - **If `judge_independent = TRUE`:** proceed to Step 4 normally — no change to existing behavior.
   - **If `judge_independent = FALSE`, or no row found (unscored — the CALL failed or Gemini returned nothing):** WITHHOLD Step 4's binding action entirely this cycle. Instead: count prior echo-suspect requeues for this review id (`SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(CAST(SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64) AS STRING), CONCAT('unkeyed:', event_id))) FROM events.queue_events WHERE queue='PENDING_REVIEW' AND item_key = <id> AND JSON_VALUE(payload, '$.echo_suspect_requeue') = 'true'`). **DISTINCT CYCLES, NOT ROWS:** marker replication must not count one retry twice.
     - **If < 2** (first or second echo-suspect finding for this review): re-enqueue a fresh cycle of the SAME review — `INSERT INTO events.queue_events` (same `item_key`/id, `queue='PENDING_REVIEW'`, `status='pending'`, `review_type` unchanged, `cycle_number` = this cycle + 1, fresh `attacker_due_date` = next trading day, `orchestrator_due_date` = one trading day after that, `payload.echo_suspect_requeue='true'`, `payload.echo_suspect_reason` = the judge's `judge_reason` or "unscored — theater judge unavailable"). This forces a genuinely FRESH attacker pass (the queue-driven AR_att routine picks it up like any other pending entry) rather than trusting the same orchestrator's already-suspect independence on a second look. Log `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='theater-quarantine'`, naming the review id + why) and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','AR_orc','echo_suspect_requeue', '<review id> — <review_type> verdict withheld, judge_independent=<v>, re-adjudication cycle <n> enqueued', '<JSON>')`. Do NOT perform ANY of Step 4's actions for this cycle — the prior binding state (activation state / strategy status) stays exactly as it was before this review started.
     - **If >= 2** (already requeued twice for echo-suspect reasons and still not independently verified): this is no longer a transient judge hiccup — escalate rather than loop forever. `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical','AR_orc','echo_suspect_cap_reached', '<review id> — <review_type> has failed the theater-independence gate 2+ times; binding action withheld; AR_orc STEP 0.5 retries up to 3 lifetime cool-off cycles (>=14 days apart), then parks permanently pending owner investigation (echo_suspect_exhausted)', '<JSON>')`, write an `events.decision_log` entry, and set the queue entry `status='complete'` with the park marker written into the row's **`note` COLUMN** — `note='echo_suspect_cap_reached — binding action withheld, escalated'`. For a `divergence-review` that row's payload also carries `resolution_kind = 'parked'` and `new_state` = the operative value left in place (Step 5's DIVERGENCE-REVIEW CLOSE PAYLOAD; D2's test (a) counts a parked review as open) (added 2026-10-19, owner decision in an interactive session: wire Strategy.md's daily technical-flip divergence clause literally). **WRITE IT TO `note`; THERE IS NO `outcome` FIELD (pinned 2026-09-13 by AR_orc's own fire — this bullet read `outcome='…'` until now).** `events.queue_events` has thirteen columns (`event_id`, `event_ts`, `queue`, `item_key`, `item_type`, `status`, `strategy`, `ticker`, `due_date`, `conservative_default`, `artifact_path`, `payload`, `note`) and no `outcome` among them, and the `PENDING_REVIEW` payload schema above enumerates its own fields with no `outcome` either — its free-form field is `notes`, i.e. the `note` column. The marker must remain detectable by STEP 0.5, the only automated recovery path. **Cite that term to its CANONICAL LIVE body, `bigquery/176_decouple_embedding_health_from_trading_gate.sql`, not to `bigquery/47_trading_enabled_resync.sql` (corrected 2026-09-15 by AR_orc's own fire):** The canonical blocking-criticals form is `COUNTIF(NOT resolved AND severity = 'critical' AND category NOT IN ('trading_halted', 'staleness') AND alert_id NOT IN (halt_echo_md) AND alert_id NOT IN (halt_echo_mr))` — the `staleness` exclusion from `bigquery/78`, the `missing_dependency` and `missed_run` halt-echo carve-outs from `bigquery/97` and `bigquery/107`. `echo_suspect_cap_reached` is outside the live carve-outs and blocks staging. STEP 0.5's detect now reads `payload.outcome` as well, so a park already written under the old wording is still found. (do NOT auto-apply the default-on-ambiguity verdict — an ambiguity default is for a genuinely inconclusive REVIEW, not for a review the independence gate itself cannot trust). No further auto-requeue.

4. Take resulting action (SKIP entirely for divergence-review / m2m-termination / strategy-retirement if Step 3.5 withheld the action this cycle):

   **STEP 4 PROVENANCE CONTRACT — binds EVERY branch below (pinned 2026-08-25 by AR_orc's own fire).** Every `events.decision_log` entry any branch of this step writes MUST carry, in `fields`: `review_id` (the queue `item_key`), `cycle_number` (the **GRADED** cycle — the one Step 3's transcript was written at, never the next one), `review_type`, `routine='AR_orc'`, and `orchestrator_event_id` (the `event_id` Step 3 returned); and every `events.queue_events` row this step enqueues MUST carry `payload.review_id` and `payload.orchestrator_event_id` alongside the `cycle_number` its own bullet specifies. Put the orchestrator transcript `event_id` and the consumed attacker `event_id` in `refs`. **These are not decoration — STEP 0's "Establish whether Step 4 landed" reads exactly these keys**, and that read is the only thing between a session that dies between Step 3 and Step 5 and either a duplicated Step 4 (non-binding types) or a `critical` `review_handoff_stuck` + `state.trading_enabled = FALSE` raised over a verdict that had in fact executed (binding types). The shape was never written down here and it drifted the moment a recovery session composed the `sp_log_decision` call by hand: MEASURED 2026-08-25, 24 of 26 Step 4 pre-mortem entries since 2026-07-31 carry `review_id` + `cycle_number`, and the two most recent (2026-08-24) carry neither, with empty `refs` and `tags`. **`decision` / `title` prose naming the review and cycle is NOT a substitute** — a reader forced to regex a free-text title silently matches nothing the first time the wording moves, the same defect class as the `artifact_moved` marker read Step 5 documents and as the `handoff_contract_unpinned` findings. State the keys, then write them. (The two 2026-08-24 entries are deliberately NOT backfilled with correction rows: both their cycles reached `complete`, so STEP 0 — which selects only at `attacker-complete` — can never read them, making a backfill pure cosmetics bought with a `superseded_by` mutation on a graded verdict.)

   **ECHO-SUSPECT COOL-OFF RESOLVE (consumption-closure audit 2026-07-16 — pairs with STEP 0.5 above).** **Establish whether this IS a cool-off cycle CYCLE-SCOPED, off `events.queue_events` directly — never off the single row this fire consumed and never off `state.open_queue` / `state.open_queue_detail` (pinned 2026-09-15 by AR_orc's own fire; MEASURED below):** `SELECT COUNTIF(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.echo_suspect_cooloff')='true' AND CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64)=<this cycle_number>) > 0 AS is_cooloff_cycle, COUNT(DISTINCT IF(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.echo_suspect_cooloff')='true' AND SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64)<=<this cycle_number>, SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64), NULL)) AS cooloff_attempt_n FROM events.queue_events WHERE queue='PENDING_REVIEW' AND item_key=<this review id>` — one query yielding both the gate and the `<n>` the resolved_note below needs, with `cooloff_attempt_n` counting DISTINCT marker CYCLES, the same unit as STEP 0.5's lifetime cap, so the two can never disagree about how many retries have happened. `is_cooloff_cycle` stays a `COUNTIF(...) > 0`, which a duplicate row cannot move. If `is_cooloff_cycle` is TRUE and Step 3.5 passed (`judge_independent=TRUE`) so this step executed: after completing the verdict's actions below (resolve last — never clear the block before the action that justifies clearing it has been taken), `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='re-adjudicated independently on cool-off retry <n> of 3; verdict executed — <review id>' WHERE category='echo_suspect_cap_reached' AND NOT resolved AND message LIKE CONCAT('%', <review id>, '%')` — the sanctioned in-place alerts resolution (same pattern as D2 Step 0's termination_close_staged resolve), clearing the trading block the capped review latched. This resolves duplicate cap rows for the same review id together, by design. It may now legitimately match ZERO rows: with STEP 0.5 keyed on the park rather than on the alert, a cool-off retry can run for a review whose cap alert was already resolved out of band — a 0-row UPDATE there is the correct no-op, not a failure, and the re-adjudication it accompanies is the substantive recovery either way. Record the passing attempt number (`<n>` = `cooloff_attempt_n` from the cycle-scoped query above, 1-3) in both the resolved_note above and the Step 4 decision_log entry — the "passed after N independence failures" audit trail (rev 2, 2026-07-16). A resolve site is its entry condition AND its UPDATE predicate; inspect both in any future sweep. Do NOT "fix" this by asking AR_att to propagate the marker forward: marker replication is not its contract — scope the READ to the cycle, at the site that owns it. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/AR_orc.md` § H-AR_orc-07.)*

   **TWO MORE AR_orc CATEGORIES HAD NO CLOSE PATH EITHER — `echo_suspect_requeue` AND `prose_regression_confirmed` (added 2026-09-21, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing AR_att's `ar_orc_notice_no_close_path`, alert `e387df56-bce7-4b81-b112-07b9e389257d`).** Both are raised by AR_orc — the first by Step 3.5's `< 2` branch, the second by Step 4's prose-regression CONFIRMED DRIFT limb — and, exactly as the clause above records for `echo_suspect_cap_reached`, **neither had an `ops.alert_policy` row, neither is reachable by `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts`, and no step of AR_orc ever resolved either**, so the first row either one ever raised would have stayed open permanently. Verified live 2026-09-21: both categories absent from `ops.alert_policy`. Both are `warning`, so unlike `echo_suspect_cap_reached` neither can latch a trading halt — this is an alert-board hygiene defect, not a capital one, and it is **latent**: `echo_suspect_requeue` has never been written (0 of 206 `PENDING_REVIEW` rows) and no `prose_regression_confirmed` row exists. Registered non-latching the same cycle, and closed here:
   - **`echo_suspect_requeue` — condition-healed, at the site that ends the condition.** The condition is "a verdict is withheld pending a fresh adjudication cycle", and it ENDS the moment that re-adjudication produces an independent verdict. So on any fire where Step 3.5 passes (`judge_independent = TRUE`) and Step 4's actions execute, AFTER those actions: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='re-adjudicated independently and verdict executed on cycle <n> (healed by AR_orc)' WHERE category='echo_suspect_requeue' AND NOT resolved AND message LIKE CONCAT('%', <review id>, '%')`. Scope by review id, never category-wide — the message names the review, so this category holds one open row PER REVIEW and a category-wide `UPDATE` would close a different review's live withholding notice. Resolve LAST, after the action that justifies it, exactly as the cool-off resolve above does. A 0-row match is the correct no-op.
   - **`prose_regression_confirmed` — a NOTICE, not a condition; close it on the NEXT fire, never the raising one. THE OPERATIVE INSTRUCTION NO LONGER LIVES HERE: it is the NOTICE-CLOSE PASS beside the RESIDUAL SWEEP at the due scan above, and it must not be moved back (moved 2026-09-22 by AR_orc's own fire — go there for the `UPDATE`, the `alert_ts` bound, the ordering rule and the measurement).** Its job is "a genuine prose regression was confirmed and the scenario's `expected` was updated", and that job is DONE once Step 4's `prose-regression-confirmed` `events.decision_log` entry and the `scenarios.yaml` correction have landed. There is no condition to observe clearing — a confirmed drift stays confirmed — so an absence test would never fire, the same shape as `wash_sale_exposure` and for the same reason. **And that is precisely why it cannot be closed from inside this step:** "on each fire" is fire cadence, while Step 4 runs only for a SELECTED, DUE entry — 13 of this routine's 57 completed fires — so siting a fire-scoped close here contradicted both its own wording and its `ops.alert_policy` `resolve_rule` (*"on the run AFTER the one that raised it"*), and left 44 fires unable to perform the only close this category has. **`echo_suspect_requeue` above STAYS here**, because it is condition-healed and the condition it watches can only end inside this step; the two are not the same kind and must not be sited alike.

   - **divergence-review:** immediately BEFORE binding, re-run DIVERGENCE-REVIEW STANDING-CYCLE PRE-CHECK Read. Standing call changed (overlapping D2 fundamental-call) → close SUPERSEDED exactly as pre-check, notice closes included, orchestrator_event_id THIS transcript; skip rest of bullet AND Step 5 close. Otherwise write binding events.regime_events STRATEGY_ACTIVATION, as_of_date state.trading_day_today.today, divergence_id item_key. Verdict differs from prior state → sp_log_decision binding entry. 5. Update the queue entry: insert a `queue_events` row (same `item_key`) with status = complete. Do not add an output-path field to the payload; `state.adversarial_reviews_current` is the durable retrieval surface. **DIVERGENCE-REVIEW CLOSE PAYLOAD (added 2026-10-19, owner decision in an interactive session: wire Strategy.md's daily technical-flip divergence clause literally).** Every `complete` row this routine writes for a `divergence-review` carries payload `resolution_kind` and `new_state`: `'verdict'` with the value Step 4 bound (here, and at STEP 0's evidence-complete path), `'moot'` or `'superseded'` from the DIVERGENCE-REVIEW STANDING-CYCLE PRE-CHECK (`'superseded'` also from Step 4's re-read), and `'parked'` at Step 3.5's `>= 2` branch, each with the `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION` value in force after it. D2's ROUTER EVERY-RUN DUTIES read both keys: only a `'verdict'` services a recurring divergence for the rest of its cycle.
   - **ARTIFACT-DRIFT NOTICE RESOLVE — the operative half of Step 1.5's withhold branch (moved here 2026-08-19, later the same evening; it was written into that branch earlier that night and was unreachable there, because the session that performs the close is a later fire that takes the gate's *equal* branch and never executes the withhold branch's bullets).** **Read the marker CYCLE-SCOPED, never row-scoped (pinned 2026-08-20 by AR_orc's own fire — see MEASURED below):** `SELECT COUNTIF(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.artifact_moved')='true') > 0 AS artifact_moved, ANY_VALUE(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.attacked_commit')) AS attacked_commit, ANY_VALUE(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.current_commit')) AS current_commit FROM events.queue_events WHERE queue='PENDING_REVIEW' AND item_key=<this review id> AND CAST(JSON_VALUE(payload,'$.cycle_number') AS INT64)=<this cycle_number>` — EVERY `queue_events` row for THIS `item_key` at THIS `cycle_number`, and specifically **not** the single row this fire consumed and **not** `state.open_queue` / `state.open_queue_detail`. If `artifact_moved` is TRUE — the marker Step 1.5's re-enqueue writes, alongside `attacked_commit` / `current_commit` — then this fire IS the graded cycle that notice was waiting for, and Step 3 has just written the verdict it was waiting on.  **The marker is a property of the CYCLE that Step 1.5's re-enqueue created, not of any one row inside it, so read it that way.** Do NOT instead fix this by asking AR_att to propagate the key forward — that makes every writer responsible for carrying every other routine's markers and fails silently the first time one is missed; scope the READ to the cycle, at the site that owns the close. The Step 0.5 lifetime count and Step 4 ECHO-SUSPECT COOL-OFF RESOLVE also read markers cycle-scoped. A future sweep must inspect both the condition that reaches each UPDATE and its predicate. Resolve it: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='re-adjudicated at cycle <this cycle_number> against <current sha>; verdict written — <review id>' WHERE category='artifact_version_drift' AND NOT resolved AND message LIKE CONCAT('%', <review id>, '%')`. Resolving every open row for the same review id together is deliberate — a review re-enqueued twice raises two rows for one condition, and one verdict discharges both. The same sanctioned in-place resolve as Step 4's echo-suspect cool-off clause and D3's `queue_item_stale` HEAL-RESOLUTION (ITEM 17 precedent). **Resolve on the marker and the written verdict, never on age** — an aged-out row would be indistinguishable from a genuinely re-adjudicated one, the aging-alert trap `phantom_run_completion` documents — and **never resolve a review id other than this entry's**: the evidence is per-review, exactly as `handoff_contract_unpinned`'s is per-handoff. A `warning` never contributes to a trading halt (every gate counts `critical` only), so this is hygiene, not a gate release — but an alert board nobody can ever clear is how a real signal gets lost in noise. Best-effort: a failure here can never abort the run or un-write the verdict. **Step 0's `Evidence complete → finish Step 5 only` reconciliation branch runs this bullet too** — a verdict stranded by a dead session still discharges its drift notice when the queue row is finally closed. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/AR_orc.md` § H-AR_orc-09.)*

CHAT OUTPUT:
- Crafted order instructions (tap-to-confirm deep link + summary) if any were staged (otherwise omit).
- One line per processed entry naming the entry id, review_type, final verdict, theater-check flag, and action taken. If multiple entries were processed this fire, list each on its own line.
- **A STEP 0 reconciliation and a STEP 0.5 cool-off action each get their OWN line too, whether or not any entry was processed (added 2026-09-16 by AR_orc's own fire; the same-day counterpart of AR_att's 2026-09-16 CHAT OUTPUT pin, and the other half of the quiet-day binding stated at the due scan above).** Both steps act BEFORE any entry is selected, so neither can ever produce a "processed entry" line and both would otherwise be invisible here — which is how a fire that halted trading could still print the quiet-day sentence. For a **STEP 0 reconciliation**: the review id, `review_type`, the cycle finished, the orchestrator transcript `event_id` the `complete` row was written against, and which branch it took (evidence complete → Step 5 finished; evidence absent + NON-binding → Step 4 replayed; evidence absent + BINDING → `review_handoff_stuck` raised and the entry deliberately LEFT at `attacker-complete`) — marked as a reconciliation of a PRIOR fire's verdict, never as a fresh one; it has no new verdict, and the verdict of record is the one already in that transcript. For a **STEP 0.5 action**: the review id, the cool-off attempt number, and whether the cycle was re-enqueued or the lifetime cap parked it permanently with `echo_suspect_exhausted` (naming, in that branch, that the `critical` blocks `state.trading_enabled` until a human clears it). **Record the same in the `sp_routine_end` `<note>`.** A repair, or a park, that leaves no trace in either place reproduces the failure those two steps exist to make visible.
- **The RESIDUAL SWEEP gets its own line on BOTH of its acting branches — the third branch the bullet above left out (added 2026-09-17 by AR_orc's own fire; see the quiet-day binding's HEAL clause at the due scan above).** Like the two steps above it, the sweep runs outside any selected entry and can never produce a "processed entry" line. On the **NAMING** branch: the count and the `item_key`s it wrote into the `review_orchestrator_due_date_unparseable` payload (never into the message, which is a fixed sentence), plus the fact that it deliberately did NOT grade those rows — a missing due date is a producer defect and grading it here would consume the attacker handoff ahead of its scheduled orchestrator day. On the **CLEAN-BUT-HEALING** branch: the `alert_id`s the condition-keyed heal resolved, named as the only automated close path that category has anywhere. A clean sweep that resolved nothing needs no line — that case, and only that case, is the genuine quiet day. **Record the same in the `sp_routine_end` `<note>`.**
- **The NOTICE-CLOSE PASS gets its own line whenever it resolves anything — the FIFTH acting branch, and the second that can fire on an otherwise-quiet day (added 2026-09-22 by AR_orc's own fire; see the pass itself at the due scan above).** Like the three steps above it, the pass runs outside any selected entry and can never produce a "processed entry" line. Name the `alert_id`s it resolved for `prose_regression_confirmed`, and name that `UPDATE` as the ONLY automated close path the category has anywhere — verified against the live bodies, neither `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` nor the `ops.sp_sq_cadence_check` #14 seven-day auto-age allowlist reaches it, and `latching=FALSE` only sanctions the resolve rather than performing it. A pass that resolved nothing needs no line; that case, together with a sweep that is both clean and non-healing, is the genuine quiet day. **Record the same in the `sp_routine_end` `<note>`.**

- One or two themes dominating market commentary

6. Earnings and fundamentals backdrop
- Aggregate beat rates and surprise magnitudes for earnings seasons within the quarter
- Change in forward S&P 500 EPS consensus
- Sector-level earnings divergences

7. Overall regime characterization (3–5 sentences)

Concentration check. **Before treating this as a hard block, read `state.strategy_capital_enablement` for D.** If `capital_disabled = TRUE`, D's idle cash is swept out under Operating_Protocols.md §16 and D's NAV converges to its own deployed book, so a %-of-NAV/%-of-book GICS reading computed in this state may not be measuring what the criterion intends — this is an open, unresolved spec question (`ops.alerts` category `sector_cap_denominator_artifact`; M3 finding F-12, `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md` 2026-09-01). **It is NOT reliably a sweep-caused, self-reversing artifact** (verified 2026-09-14 against the prior M3 cycle's own recorded figures, `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md` git history 2026-08-03: Industrials already read 35.04% of D's then-$532.82 deployed book — three days before the 2026-08-06 capital-disable sweep this finding otherwise blames, and unaffected by it, since capital restoration changes NAV, not book composition), and reconciling which denominator Strategy.md's entry criterion 5 actually specifies is an A3/owner-level entry-criterion question, not one this routine may resolve. In that state, still compute and report the reading for the candidate's writeup, but do NOT classify the candidate "blocked by concentration" on it alone — classify readiness from the candidate's other criteria and carry the concentration reading as a flagged caveat rather than a block. When D is capital-enabled (the normal case), compare against current D book as before: does adding this name push any GICS sector above 30% concentration? Note the implication. (Strategy.md entry criterion 5; the former "max 3 concurrent positions per GICS sector" headcount variant is REMOVED per Rev 35, owner directive — only the 30%-of-NAV exposure form remains.)

5. Correlation-bucket check (monitoring only — corrected 2026-07-15 per Strategy.md Rev 35, owner directive: the bucket-size cap AND its entry-blocking consequence are REMOVED, not just the separate "10-concurrent-position hard cap" this replaced on 2026-07-03). Per Strategy.md entry criterion 5: compute trailing-252-day daily-return correlation between this candidate and each currently-held D position (classical-method delegation — code, not eyeballed). Any pair exceeding 0.6 correlation shares a "bucket"; report bucket membership/size for Section 6 informational tracking — it no longer blocks entry or forces any exit, regardless of bucket size.

6. Momentum screen. Is the name rallying hard (specify magnitude) in the trailing 30 days? Flag for entry deferral per Strategy.md.

Rank shortlist of up to 10 candidates for full thesis construction. Per candidate:
- Thesis strength (ordinal rating, with reasoning)
- Specific catalysts or drivers
- Specific invalidation criteria
- Current sector concentration implication (the one remaining live blocking check) AND correlation-bucket status (informational only, Rev 35 — not a blocking check)
- Readiness (ready now / deferred pending rally pause / blocked by concentration)

Exclude names in the open D book. Note any shortlist addition that would require an existing D position to close first — do not recommend the close.

OUTPUT: write the complete content (PART 1 + PART 2) directly to `Quarterly_D_Candidates.md`. First line is the YYYY-QN marker. Chat output: one-line acknowledgment.

A general paper whose panel happens to include a Claude model is L2/L3 evidence; check panels rather than assuming L4.

Frame research adversarially: look for evidence that contradicts or updates documented edges and disadvantages, not evidence that confirms them. Offsets self-reference bias (this task evaluates LLM claims while being executed by an LLM).

New research on documented disadvantages and any newly-identified failure modes. Include replications. Per item: models evaluated. Flag items that evaluated a Claude model specifically or that claim architectural generality.

AI adoption, retail AI use, AI share of trading volume, capital concentration through specific foundation models. Synchronized AI-driven market events. Regulator reports.

Section 5 — Adversarial content and manipulation risks
Prompt injection research, adversarial content targeting AI consumption, AI-generated content in financial documents. Per item: models evaluated where relevant.

Section 6 — Regulatory developments affecting AI in financial decision-making
New regulations, consultations, enforcement actions affecting AI-driven trading, robo-advisory, algorithmic decision-making.

Six sections, reverse chronological within each, citations inline.

PART 2 — Verification answers and per-strategy effects. Answer each AI_Trading_Foundation.md Part 4 verification question explicitly using PART 1 as evidence. Default bias: YES — err toward flagging change, err toward triggering per-strategy foundation-change assessment. The experiment accepts false-positive assessments to catch real changes.

Transferability filter for non-Claude evidence. For PART 1 findings drawn from models other than Claude (Sections 2, 3, 5), a finding triggers per-strategy foundation-change assessment only if at least one of the following is present: (a) replication on a Claude model, (b) architectural generality — the mechanism is a documented property of autoregressive LLMs broadly rather than a specific model's training artifact, or (c) evidence from an Anthropic-family model (prior Claude version). Non-Claude findings lacking transferability evidence are logged in the YES/NO answer and flagged as watch items for the next review cycle, but do not trigger foundation-change assessment on their own.
